item.title: SEC fines Tennessee $250K after fans disrupted game vs. LSU by throwing golf balls and mustard
item.description: Tennessee has been fined $250,000 by the Southeastern Conference for fan conduct that disrupted Saturday’s game against LSU, the conference announced Sunday. Fans at Neyland Stadium threw golf balls and mustard onto the field during the fourth quarter of the No. 9 Volunteers’ win over Lane Kiffin’s Tigers , leading the teams to stop play for a few minutes. In a statement, the SEC said that the fine was assessed due to fans “throwing debris” onto the field, interrupting the game and “endangering contest participants.” The SEC appeared to justify the fine with a bylaw referring to the availability of alcohol, saying that the conference can fine the school “if cans or plastic bottles are used as projectiles or otherwise cause game management issues.” The SEC is also able to suspended the university’s ability to sell alcohol at games, though it says that it does not plan to do so at this time. The choice to throw golf balls and mustard was not by coincidence: The seemingly random combination is connected to the school’s previous history with Kiffin. Tennessee’s hatred of the LSU coach stems from Kiffin’s brief stint as head coach of the Vols in 2009, before Kiffin left to coach USC after just one year. In 2021, Kiffin returned to Neyland Stadium for the first time, then coaching Ole Miss. He was greeted with Tennessee fans who threw random debris, including golf balls and a mustard bottle. At SEC media days, Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel encouraged fans to reprise the moment when LSU came to Neyland. “I certainly hope our fan base hasn’t cooled off,” Heupel said at the time. “Whether it’s the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard, or our sports stores making sure that they’ve got reinforcements on the golf balls, hopefully Knoxville is ready for his arrival.” Volunteers fans happily took the challenge. In addition to bringing the specific items to throw at the LSU bench, several fans also wore mustard bottles in the stands while cheering Tennessee to a 27-13 win. A Tennessee field crew member carries a mustard bottle and golf balls off the field at Neyland Stadium. (Randy Sartin-Imagn Images) IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS Kiffin, for what it’s worth, took the situation in stride. “They listened to their coach,” Kiffin said postgame. “I'm not being critical of him, I'm laughing at it.”
item.dc:creator: Kari Anderson

item.title: Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur gives Carson Beck injury update after missing Chiefs game
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur gives Carson Beck injury update after missing Chiefs game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals took the field against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11. However, they went into this game without rookie Carson Beck under center. Veteran Josh Johnson was the starter on Sunday, with Beck sitting on the sidelines. Beck missed Sunday’s game with a back injury. Johnson took over the offense, but couldn’t lead Arizona to a win. The Chiefs won on Sunday, and Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur spoke about Beck’s injury after the loss . “They’re back spasms. There’s no magic pill you can take for that. You just treat it, and kind of go from there. Obviously kept him back for obvious reasons… We kept Carson back because we didn’t think it was beneficial for anyone to bring him here,” the Cardinals head coach said, via PHNX Cardinals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Johnson turned in a solid performance for Arizona, tossing one touchdown pass and racking up 155 yards through the air. He did not throw an interception, either. Johnson did fumble once, but it was recovered by the Cardinals. Still, Arizona had no answer for Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs offense. Mahomes threw for 324 yards while also throwing three touchdown passes. Kansas City improved to 8-2 on the season with its 34-7 victory over the Cardinals on Sunday. Arizona is looking to find some sort of positive momentum in a lost season. One thing that could swing their way is getting Beck back healthy. The Cardinals drafted him in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Seeing what he can do on the field is important for the team’s near- and long-term future. Arizona will look to get back in the win column on November 29 when they take on the Washington Commanders. item.title: Full Card Revealed For ONE Friday Fights 180 On November 27
item.description: ONE Championship closes out November with a fresh slate of martial arts action at Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, live in Asia primetime on Friday, November 27. ONE Friday Fights 180 features nine bouts across Muay Thai, kickboxing, and MMA, with the athletes chasing the US$100,000 contract and a spot on ONE’s main roster. In the main event, Denkriangkrai Mavinn Muaythai adds another chapter to his long Lumpinee Stadium resume when he meets Myanmar’s Thway Lin Htet in a strawweight Muay Thai contest. The 27-year-old southpaw grew up training at his uncle’s gym, which was built inside a rubber plantation, and he has since become one of the most battle-tested athletes on the weekly series. A former Omnoi Stadium Champion who draws inspiration from his Team Mavinn Muaythai teammate Shadow Mavinn , he owns 10 victories in ONE and is known for a lethal left body kick and a sharp fight IQ. Most recently, he earned a unanimous decision over Abdessamie Rhenimi at ONE Friday Fights 166 . Photo credit: ONE Championship Standing across from him, the 23-year-old Thway Lin Htet is a Lethwei Champion who has built a reputation for highlight-reel finishes. He knocked out Kritpet PK Saenchai with a spinning elbow at ONE Friday Fights 112 and stopped two-time Lumpinee Stadium Muay Thai World Champion Chokpreecha PK Saenchai by second-round TKO at ONE Friday Fights 121 . The Phyo Wai Group representative arrives off a split-decision win over Xavier Gonzalez at ONE Friday Fights 170 , and his forward-marching style and explosive power make him a threat to end any night early. In the co-main event, Nuatoranee Jitmuangnon returns to ONE Friday Fights to take on Yodchanachai Tor Pitakchai in an atomweight Muay Thai bout. The 28-year-old Thai last stepped into the ONE ring at ONE Friday Fights 8 in 2023, and he comes back after more than three years away with a fresh opportunity to make his mark on the weekly series. Yodchanachai, who will be making his ONE debut, will look to make an impression in the opposite corner. ONE Friday Fights 180 Full Card Denkriangkrai Mavinn Muaythai vs. Thway Lin Htet (Muay Thai – strawweight) Nuatoranee Jitmuangnon vs. Yodchanachai Tor Pitakchai (Muay Thai – atomweight) Saencherngnoi Tor Muangsema vs. Petthanawat Sor Jaruwan (Muay Thai – featherweight) Jaxson Hayman vs. Sixten Larsson (Muay Thai – lightweight) Alistair Fitzharris vs. Bhupen Mutum (MMA – flyweight) Panpet Sor Dechapan vs. Youssef Erraji (Muay Thai – flyweight) Arti Khatri vs. Norika Ryu (MMA – atomweight) Efe Caliskan vs. Fuga Onodera (Muay Thai – featherweight) Chen Jiayi vs. Taku Takaiwa (kickboxing – flyweight) Source

item.title: 3 Things We Learned As Heat Overwhelm Thunder To Log Seventh Consecutive Victory
item.description: Nov 22, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Miami Heat center Bam Adebayo (13) protects the basketball against Oklahoma City Thunder forward Brooks Barnhizer (23) during the fourth quarter at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat entered Sunday night’s game with a full head of steam after securing a noteworthy victory over the Milwaukee Bucks . Despite Giannis Antetokounmpo ‘s absence, the Heat showcased their potential, as they beat the Oklahoma City Thunder 123-113 to extend their winning streak to seven games. Sunday’s win over the Thunder is a particularly meaningful one for Miami. Even with Antetokounmpo’s sidelined , the Heat showcased their resilience and their ability to maintain their overall production. To that end, even though the scoring charge was led by Bam Adebayo and Pelle Larsson , the efforts of the remaining players cannot be overlooked. In all fairness, like the Heat, even the Thunder fielded a shorthanded rotation, as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was ruled out for the game. Still, considering how deep OKC’s roster is, which was highlighted by the performances of Jared McCain (20 PTS, 2 REB, 3 AST) and Bennett Stirtz (21 PTS, 3 REB, 5 AST, 5-12 3PT), the Heat deserve credit for not taking their foot off the gas. As Miami improves to 10-6 on the season after this win, it is difficult to ignore the team’s rise. On that note, we examine the three things we learned from Sunday night’s performance. Bam Adebayo Proved He’s Capable Of Taking Over Games One of the most important factors heading into Sunday’s game was Bam Adebayo. With Giannis Antetokounmpo ruled out of the matchup, Adebayo was tasked with the role of serving as the offensive focal point and the defensive anchor. In many ways, this implied a reprisal of his role last year. Sadly, he has not looked very comfortable in this position this season. Despite his early-season struggles with asserting himself on offense, Bam Adebayo seemed to have found his groove against the Thunder. With a noteworthy performance of 24 points (game-high), 15 rebounds, and 12 assists, which included two blocks and two steals, Adebayo truly lived up to his status as Miami’s franchise cornerstone. Unlike most games, Adebayo came out firing in the first quarter itself. By asserting himself on the interior by constantly battling for rebounds and scoring around the rim, the Heat superstar created several opportunities for Miami to develop an offensive rhythm. Needless to say, this paid off, as the team comfortably scored 36 points in the opening frame. Although the team’s effort trailed off at times, Bam Adebayo came through at crucial points to help Miami remain in front. Even though such performances are an expectation from him, seeing him step up to the plate in this fashion was quite reassuring. item.content:encoded: Nov 22, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Miami Heat center Bam Adebayo (13) protects the basketball against Oklahoma City Thunder forward Brooks Barnhizer (23) during the fourth quarter at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat entered Sunday night’s game with a full head of steam after securing a noteworthy victory over the Milwaukee Bucks . Despite Giannis Antetokounmpo ‘s absence, the Heat showcased their potential, as they beat the Oklahoma City Thunder 123-113 to extend their winning streak to seven games. Sunday’s win over the Thunder is a particularly meaningful one for Miami. Even with Antetokounmpo’s sidelined , the Heat showcased their resilience and their ability to maintain their overall production. To that end, even though the scoring charge was led by Bam Adebayo and Pelle Larsson , the efforts of the remaining players cannot be overlooked. In all fairness, like the Heat, even the Thunder fielded a shorthanded rotation, as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was ruled out for the game. Still, considering how deep OKC’s roster is, which was highlighted by the performances of Jared McCain (20 PTS, 2 REB, 3 AST) and Bennett Stirtz (21 PTS, 3 REB, 5 AST, 5-12 3PT), the Heat deserve credit for not taking their foot off the gas. As Miami improves to 10-6 on the season after this win, it is difficult to ignore the team’s rise. On that note, we examine the three things we learned from Sunday night’s performance. Bam Adebayo Proved He’s Capable Of Taking Over Games One of the most important factors heading into Sunday’s game was Bam Adebayo. With Giannis Antetokounmpo ruled out of the matchup, Adebayo was tasked with the role of serving as the offensive focal point and the defensive anchor. In many ways, this implied a reprisal of his role last year. Sadly, he has not looked very comfortable in this position this season. Despite his early-season struggles with asserting himself on offense, Bam Adebayo seemed to have found his groove against the Thunder. With a noteworthy performance of 24 points (game-high), 15 rebounds, and 12 assists, which included two blocks and two steals, Adebayo truly lived up to his status as Miami’s franchise cornerstone. Unlike most games, Adebayo came out firing in the first quarter itself. By asserting himself on the interior by constantly battling for rebounds and scoring around the rim, the Heat superstar created several opportunities for Miami to develop an offensive rhythm. Needless to say, this paid off, as the team comfortably scored 36 points in the opening frame. Although the team’s effort trailed off at times, Bam Adebayo came through at crucial points to help Miami remain in front. Even though such performances are an expectation from him, seeing him step up to the plate in this fashion was quite reassuring. Davion Mitchell Should Not Be Underestimated Another player who deserves his flowers after Sunday night’s performance is Heat guard Davion Mitchell . After Tyler Herro was traded to the Bucks, it became apparent that Mitchell would have greater responsibilities to deal with. Even though he underwent grueling training in the offseason to embrace this role, many doubted his abilities. Now, the guard seems to be proving naysayers wrong. Davion Mitchell was one of the most impactful players for the Heat on Sunday night. Although he didn’t lead the team in scoring, logging 14 points on 5-10 shooting from the field, his four rebounds and three assists were quite remarkable. To some extent, many may exaggerate his four turnovers for the game, one of which came off a high-risk pass to the corner early in the third quarter. While such criticism would be justified, it negates how well Mitchell conducted Miami’s offense. Mitchell routinely established himself as a scoring threat before switching back to distributing the ball. In light of this systematic and organized approach to breaking down defenses, there is a lot to like about the guard’s development. In that regard, his averages of 17.4 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 9.0 assists only capture why the 28-year-old should not be underestimated. The Heat Are Deeper Than They Look On paper, the Heat have a phenomenal roster. Aside from having players like Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, Miami also features other familiar faces like Klay Thompson . While impressive, this gives the impression that the Heat are a top-heavy team. Sunday night’s performance suggested otherwise. Although Adebayo led the scoring charge with 24 points, Miami saw consistent contributions across the board. With seven players logging double-digit scoring on the night, the team clearly has more depth than expected. Despite his potential, Pelle Larsson has struggled to find his footing on offense. But against the Thunder, Larsson looked more assured, logging 21 points, three rebounds, and five assists on 9-14 shooting from the field, serving as a key scoring option behind Adebayo. Another name that stood on the Heat’s team sheet was Nikola Jovic . While it is a well-known fact that the forward has faced challenges with meeting expectations , the 23-year-old shone on Sunday night, posting an efficient 15 points, eight rebounds, and three assists on 4-8 shooting from the field with 3-6 from deep. Given what he is capable of, the Heat will hope Jovic can use this performance as a stepping stone to find his rhythm. All things considered, Sunday night’s performance provided some reassurance about the Heat’s roster depth. Hence, even though the team will fall short of expectations on some nights, knowing that there are players who can turn things up a notch when their number is called should instill Miami with even more confidence in its ability to compete.

item.title: "Where's That Replay Assist Guy?": J.J. Watt Calls Out NFL Official During CBS Broadcast After Controversial Giants-Jaguars Incident
item.description: October 1, 2023: J.J. Watt speaks to the crowd during his induction into the Houston Texans Ring of Honor during a game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Houston Texans in Houston, TX. .. /CSM USA – ZUMAc04_ 20231001_zma_c04_278 Copyright: xTraskxSmithx ©IMAGO/ZUMA Wire Replay assist played a massive role in the Jaguars’ loss against the Giants. The team ended up with a 23-18 defeat, but several officiating decisions made the game difficult for Jacksonville. The controversial calls even prompted CBS Sports analyst J.J. Watt to share his opinion during the broadcast. J.J. Watt : “Where’s that replay assist guy? Come on in, buddy.” Then Jim Nantz added to it, saying: “He went out to get a bacon, egg, and cheese.” J.J. Watt: “He might be selling ’em after that. Yeah, that ball was on the ground. Yeah, no question. No, I think that’s fairly clear. Although, what do I know?” J.J. Watt's on-air frustration reveals the replay system's blind spots. Stay tuned to EssentiallySports for the analysis that cuts through NFL officiating controversies. Both commentators were reacting to an incident in the third quarter. With 1:03 left in the quarter, Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy threw a deep pass intended for Malik Fields. Jaguars defensive back A.J. Johnson appeared to intercept it at the Giants’ 40-yard line, but the replay official reviewed the play and overturned the call, ruling it an incomplete pass. The Giants kept possession. However, Watt and Nantz were also mocking the replay-assist official because of an earlier decision that had created problems for Jacksonville. The Jaguars faced another controversial decision with 15:00 left in the second quarter. On third-and-2, running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. ran for two yards and was initially given a first down. Officials placed the ball past the first-down line and moved the chains. However, before Jacksonville could run its next play, replay officials stepped in and ruled that Rodriguez had not gained enough yards. Officials then moved the ball back, taking away the first down. Head coach Liam Coen challenged the decision, and the review proved him right. Slow-motion footage showed Rodriguez stretching the ball past the first-down line before his knee touched the ground. So, it made it clear that the replay assistant had incorrectly changed it. Another issue came in the fourth quarter. Jacksonville head coach Liam Coen challenged the decision, hoping to have it changed to a completed catch. However, after reviewing the play, officials stuck with their original ruling. Referee Craig Wrolstad gave a brief explanation, saying, “After review, it is an incomplete pass.” Washington initially bobbled the ball in the air but appeared to gain control before his feet touched the ground. Come on in, buddy.” Then Jim Nantz added to it, saying: “He went out to get a bacon, egg, and cheese.” J.J. Watt: “He might be selling ’em after that. Yeah, that ball was on the ground. Yeah, no question. No, I think that’s fairly clear. Although, what do I know?” J.J. Watt's on-air frustration reveals the replay system's blind spots. Stay tuned to EssentiallySports for the analysis that cuts through NFL officiating controversies. Both commentators were reacting to an incident in the third quarter. With 1:03 left in the quarter, Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy threw a deep pass intended for Malik Fields. Jaguars defensive back A.J. Johnson appeared to intercept it at the Giants’ 40-yard line, but the replay official reviewed the play and overturned the call, ruling it an incomplete pass. The Giants kept possession. However, Watt and Nantz were also mocking the replay-assist official because of an earlier decision that had created problems for Jacksonville. The Jaguars faced another controversial decision with 15:00 left in the second quarter. On third-and-2, running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. ran for two yards and was initially given a first down. Officials placed the ball past the first-down line and moved the chains. However, before Jacksonville could run its next play, replay officials stepped in and ruled that Rodriguez had not gained enough yards. Officials then moved the ball back, taking away the first down. Head coach Liam Coen challenged the decision, and the review proved him right. Slow-motion footage showed Rodriguez stretching the ball past the first-down line before his knee touched the ground. So, it made it clear that the replay assistant had incorrectly changed it. Another issue came in the fourth quarter. With 12:26 left, Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw a pass to Parker Washington near the end zone, but officials ruled it incomplete. Jacksonville head coach Liam Coen challenged the decision, hoping to have it changed to a completed catch. However, after reviewing the play, officials stuck with their original ruling. Referee Craig Wrolstad gave a brief explanation, saying, “After review, it is an incomplete pass.” Washington initially bobbled the ball in the air but appeared to gain control before his feet touched the ground. The ball moved in his hands as he landed, but he did not appear to lose control of it. Even so, officials did not change their ruling. The Jaguars lost their second timeout, and the game continued with third-and-9 at the Giants’ 12-yard line. Even CBS officiating analyst Gene Steratore disagreed with the decision, saying, “I do not think he lost possession of the football.” With these officiating issues, the Jaguars suffered a loss against the Giants, raising questions about the decisions made by the officials throughout the game. item.title: Raiders TE woes continue as Michael Mayer suffers injury scare with Brock Bowers already out
item.description: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Raiders TE woes continue as Michael Mayer suffers injury scare with Brock Bowers already out appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Las Vegas Raiders scratched All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers before facing the Denver Broncos Sunday . Now Michael Mayer adds one more scare, arriving during the 38-24 loss at Empower Field. Mayer left with a back injury during the fourth quarter. He ultimately became listed as questionable . Bowers already dealt with foot and ankle injuries from the Seattle Seahawks loss the previous week. The Raiders and coach Klint Kubiak entered the Rocky Mountains with a depleted TE room. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mayer and Ian Thomas emerged as the tight end options for Vegas. The latter caught one 19-yard reception during the game. Mayer settled for one catch and four yards, as he primarily became used as a blocker. Mayer’s presence there certainly benefitted running back Ashton Jeanty , who tallied 11 carries for 79 yards. Jeanty also broke off a 46-yard run that sparked the Raiders’ rally during the second quarter. Fellow running back Mike Washington Jr. helped spell Jeanty, tallying nine carries for 42 yards. Quarterback Fernando Mendoza took off running too, handling four carries for 22 yards. Vegas finished with 143 rushing yards on the evening. The Raiders leaned mostly into Mendoza’s arm to get back into the game. The rookie even completed seven straight passes before a costly interception helped seal the Denver victory, with Ja’Quan McMillian grabbing the pick six and taking it back 35 yards. Vegas is watching its season fade away, as the Denver loss now makes the Raiders 4-7 overall. Denver continues to keep up with the AFC West division leading Kansas City Chiefs, now moving to 8-2 overall. item.title: Jaguars offense gets an F for a sloppy, clunky effort in loss to Giants
item.description: Grading the Jacksonville Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the New York Giants on Nov. 22 in East Rutherford, N.J. The Jaguars (7-3) will return home after three road games in a row to host the Tennessee Titans on Nov. 29 at EverBank Stadium. Offense: F Yuck. Start with nine offensive penalties, including four false starts by four players. There was an illegal formation, an illegal shift, a delay penalty and quarterback Trevor Lawrence came through with an oldie, but never a goodie, throwing a pass beyond the line of scrimmage ... and it wasn't close. Lawrence had three interceptions if you count the one on a two-point conversion attempt (it's not) and many of his incompletions were high. He was sacked three times and was hit eight other times. The running game struggled because the Giants' defensive line overpowered the Jags offensive line. It was a basic as football gets. The Jaguars scored only one touchdown in six trips to the red zone against a defense that had given up touchdowns on 80 percent of their oppositions' trips inside the 20-yard line. What else? How about 5 of 15 on third down (failing to convert on their first seven when it was third-and-eight or longer) and failing to punch the ball in after two shots with 2 yards to go in the third quarter? It was a mess. Defense: B This was a borderline A until the Giants' last possession, when the Jags absolutely, positively had to get the ball back with 3:40 left in the game and only one time out left. But J.J. McCarthy his Malachi Fields for 19 yards and Cam Skattebo ran for two 5-yard gains to give the Giants a first down at the two-minute warning, enabling the victory formation. Also detracting from the final grade was losing contain on McCarthy, who had a 22-yard scramble on third-and-five and a 13-yard gain on third-and-eight. He had another 29-yard run nullified by a penalty. Other than that, the Jaguars' defense played well enough to give the offense a chance. The Jaguars failed to score after Antonio Harrison's 42-yard fumble return and a missed 32-yard field goal by Dominic Zvada. Josh Hines-Allen had his first solo sack since the opening game of the season but McCarthy got hit only three other times. Skattebo was no factor until the final possession (14 carries, 34 yards, 2.4 yards per attempt) and McCarthy threw some terrible passes, with a final rating of 69.3. Malik Nabers got a TD pass but was otherwise invisible and tight end Isaiah Likely caught only one pass. It was a big one, 35 yards, but went for naught when Zavada hooked his field-goal attempt. Special teams: C For the third game in a row, Cam Little made all four of his field goal attempts, and he's made 18 in a row and 22 of 24 this season. Ameer Abdullah gave the Jaguars great field position with a 47-yard return of the opening kickoff but after getting a first down to the Giants' 14, the offense stalled and Little kicked his first field goal. The Jags struggled to cover Xavier Gipson on kickoff returns and he had a 27-yard pun

The Jaguars (7-3) will return home after three road games in a row to host the Tennessee Titans on Nov. 29 at EverBank Stadium. Offense: F Yuck. Start with nine offensive penalties, including four false starts by four players. There was an illegal formation, an illegal shift, a delay penalty and quarterback Trevor Lawrence came through with an oldie, but never a goodie, throwing a pass beyond the line of scrimmage ... and it wasn't close. Lawrence had three interceptions if you count the one on a two-point conversion attempt (it's not) and many of his incompletions were high. He was sacked three times and was hit eight other times. The running game struggled because the Giants' defensive line overpowered the Jags offensive line. It was a basic as football gets. The Jaguars scored only one touchdown in six trips to the red zone against a defense that had given up touchdowns on 80 percent of their oppositions' trips inside the 20-yard line. What else? How about 5 of 15 on third down (failing to convert on their first seven when it was third-and-eight or longer) and failing to punch the ball in after two shots with 2 yards to go in the third quarter? It was a mess. Defense: B This was a borderline A until the Giants' last possession, when the Jags absolutely, positively had to get the ball back with 3:40 left in the game and only one time out left. But J.J. McCarthy his Malachi Fields for 19 yards and Cam Skattebo ran for two 5-yard gains to give the Giants a first down at the two-minute warning, enabling the victory formation. Also detracting from the final grade was losing contain on McCarthy, who had a 22-yard scramble on third-and-five and a 13-yard gain on third-and-eight. He had another 29-yard run nullified by a penalty. Other than that, the Jaguars' defense played well enough to give the offense a chance. The Jaguars failed to score after Antonio Harrison's 42-yard fumble return and a missed 32-yard field goal by Dominic Zvada. Josh Hines-Allen had his first solo sack since the opening game of the season but McCarthy got hit only three other times. Skattebo was no factor until the final possession (14 carries, 34 yards, 2.4 yards per attempt) and McCarthy threw some terrible passes, with a final rating of 69.3. Malik Nabers got a TD pass but was otherwise invisible and tight end Isaiah Likely caught only one pass. It was a big one, 35 yards, but went for naught when Zavada hooked his field-goal attempt. Special teams: C For the third game in a row, Cam Little made all four of his field goal attempts, and he's made 18 in a row and 22 of 24 this season. Ameer Abdullah gave the Jaguars great field position with a 47-yard return of the opening kickoff but after getting a first down to the Giants' 14, the offense stalled and Little kicked his first field goal. The Jags struggled to cover Xavier Gipson on kickoff returns and he had a 27-yard punt return that gave New York prime field position to get Zvada's 51-yard field goal to take a 20-6 halftime lead. Intantibles: D Until the offense was able to finally get some points in the fourth quarter, the Jaguars were failing their first test under the bright lights, in the nation's largest media market, and failing miserably. They had their third game this season with 100 or more yards in penalties, a week after getting called only twice for 20 yards, and otherwise did not seem up to the moment. They did put together a nice comeback, scoring three times in the fourth quarter, but the defense, which had limited the Giants and McCarthy to 11 yards of offense and 1 for 11 passing on the previous four possessions, let the Giants get the two first downs they needed to run out the clock. There are always going to be detractors about Coen's thinking when it comes to situational down-and-distance and scoring, and it's the easiest thing in the world to second-guess. But had Coen taken the sure field goal on fourth-and-one at the Giants' 11 in the third quarter, the score is 20-9. Little added another field goal early in the fourth quarter. That makes it 20-12. Then Brian Thomas Jrs.' touchdown made it 20-18 and it's a no-brainer to go for two there. When it's made or not, Little kicked his final field goal with 3:40 left, which might have been the game-winner had Coen taken the easy points earlier. However, Coen has proved, if nothing else, that he's going to roll the dice and not apologize for it. Bottom line is that the Jaguars should have executed on third-and-two and fourth-and-one on the third-quarter possession, and they didn't. item.title: Photos: Best images from Thunder's 123-113 loss to Heat
item.description: The Oklahoma City Thunder punted in a 123-113 loss to the Miami Heat on Sunday. Once Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Giannis Antetokounmpo were ruled out, that ended any intrigue in a matchup between two two-time MVP winners. Ajay Mitchell struggled with 17 points and three assists. Jared McCain helped with 20 points and three assists. Bennett Stirtz had a new career-high with 21 points and five assists. Meanwhile, Bam Adebayo logged a 24-point, 15-rebound and 12-assist triple-double. Pelle Larsson had 21 points and five assists. Nikola Jovic tallied 15 points and eight rebounds. item.title: SEC Rivalry Week Schedule Sets Up a Dramatic Finish With Plenty at Stake
item.description: Alabama Crimson Tide defensive back Bray Hubbard (18) celebrates his interception as Auburn Tigers take on Alabama Crimson Tide in the Iron Bowl at Jordan-Hare Stadium in Auburn, Ala. on Saturday, Nov. 29, 2025. Alabama Crimson Tide defeated Auburn Tigers 27-20. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) BIRMINGHAM, Ala. — The Southeastern Conference has saved some of its most anticipated matchups for last. Rivalry Week arrives Friday, Nov. 27, with conference championship implications, postseason positioning and decades of bad blood sharing the spotlight. Georgia has already secured its place in the SEC Championship Game. However, Alabama, Tennessee and Texas still have unfinished business. Meanwhile, several other programs have an opportunity to close their seasons with bragging rights that last considerably longer than one Saturday. Complete SEC Rivalry Week schedule All times Eastern. Date Matchup Time TV Friday, Nov. 27 Mississippi State at Ole Miss Noon ABC Friday, Nov. 27 Florida at Florida State 3:30 p.m. ABC Friday, Nov. 27 Texas at Texas A&M 7:30 p.m. ABC Saturday, Nov. 28 Louisville at Kentucky Noon ESPN2 Saturday, Nov. 28 LSU at Arkansas 12:45 p.m. SEC Network Saturday, Nov. 28 South Carolina at Clemson 3 or 3:30 p.m. ESPN, ESPN2 or ACC Network Saturday, Nov. 28 Georgia Tech at Georgia 3:30 p.m. ABC Saturday, Nov. 28 Oklahoma at Missouri 4:15 p.m. SEC Network Saturday, Nov. 28 Tennessee at Vanderbilt 7 p.m. ESPN Saturday, Nov. 28 Auburn at Alabama 7:30 p.m. ABC South Carolina-Clemson’s exact kickoff time and television assignment remain among the options listed by the conference. Friday could change everything Texas visits Texas A&M on Friday night, giving the Longhorns the first opportunity to influence the SEC Championship Game race. A victory would improve Texas to 7-2 in conference play and place pressure on Alabama and Tennessee entering Saturday. However, a loss would eliminate the Longhorns from contention for the conference title game. Earlier Friday, Ole Miss hosts Mississippi State in the Egg Bowl. Florida also travels to Tallahassee for its annual meeting with Florida State. Saturday brings the biggest decisions Georgia hosts Georgia Tech in Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate, although the Bulldogs have already completed their SEC schedule. Meanwhile, Tennessee visits Vanderbilt before Alabama hosts Auburn in the Iron Bowl. Those two games could determine which team joins Georgia in Atlanta on Dec. 5. Elsewhere, Oklahoma travels to Missouri, South Carolina visits Clemson and Kentucky hosts Louisville. The regular season has produced plenty of surprises. Nevertheless, Rivalry Week has a way of making everything that happened before it feel like an opening act. For the SEC, the final weekend promises more than bragging rights. It will help determine the conference’s championship matchup and shape its playoff representation. Check out Week 13 College Football scores here: View our latest SEC Country articles here:

item.title: 49ers’ Colton McKivitz suffers horrifying leg injury in Mexico City
item.description: San Francisco 49ers offensive lineman Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome injury during Sunday’s game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. McKivitz — who had played in 77 straight games entering the game — seemed to snap his lower leg while blocking during a play. San Francisco 49ers offensive lineman Colton McKivitz suffered an injury against the Minnesota Vikings. (@MLFootball) The broadcast showed his left foot seemingly twisted to the side before cutting to a timeout. When they returned, many 49ers players were visibly shaken up and taking a knee. It is way too early to tell exactly what happened to the 30-year-old lineman. But there’s no doubt that this was a very serious injury. HEARTBREAKING FOOTAGE #49ers STANDOUT TACKLE COLTON MCKIVITZ JUST SUFFERED A HORRIFIC INJURY ON THE FIELD. MCKIVITZ IMMEDIATELY WENT DOWN, GRABBING AT HIS INJURY AND SCREAMING IN PAIN. TRENT WILLIAMS HAD AN EMOTIONAL OUTBURST WATCHING THE SCENE UNFOLD. pic.twitter.com/QgkfGnujwe — MLFootball (@MLFootball) November 23, 2026 A close-up of Colton McKivitz’s injury during the San Francisco 49ers-Minnesota Vikings game. (X/@MLFootball). This is a tough loss for the 49ers, who have one of the league’s best offensive lines. But the hope right now is that McKivitz’s injury isn’t as bad as it looked. There is surely more to come on his injury’s severity.

item.title: Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol after Chargers’ Week 11 loss to Jets
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol after Chargers’ Week 11 loss to Jets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers were sent crashing back to earth after losing to the New York Jets, 27-24 , at SoFi Stadium on Sunday. All the high from the Chargers’ win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 10 was erased, and it could be more costly, as Herbert was placed in concussion protocol. He played the entire game without exiting for a sideline evaluation. The Chargers have not specified the exact play on which he got hurt. The 28-year-old quarterback did not face the media , as noted by KTLA’s Hayley Elwood. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Justin Herbert is in the concussion protocol per Chargers PR. He will not be speaking postgame,” wrote Elwood on X. Herbert absorbed significant punishment against the Jets, taking six sacks and eight hits. He suffered a smack to the facemask from David Bailey in the second quarter, which drew a roughing-the-passer call. The two-time Pro Bowler threw 15-of-21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns. He also scored on a short rush to end the first half. The Chargers remained winless at home and fell to 1-9. The Jets, meanwhile, broke their five-game losing streak to the Chargers and improved to 3-8. The much-hyped pairing of Herbert and Mike McDaniel has not worked, and Los Angeles is in danger of missing the playoffs for the second time in four years. If Herbert is unable to clear the concussion protocol before Week 12 against the New England Patriots, DJ Uiagalelei is next in line to start, with Trey Lance out with a groin injury and Jake Browning on the practice squad. item.title: Jalen Smith doing it all as Bulls attempts to right ship
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images Jalen Smith doing it all as Bulls attempts to right ship appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bulls are looking to bounce back. They just went on an eight-game losing streak. Plus, they lost Caleb Wilson to a broken hand for at least six weeks. On Sunday, they welcomed the Denver Nuggets to complete a week in which they played four games. With Nic Claxton out with an illness , Jalen Smith once again filled in at center. And it was a good thing, even though he was listed as probable due to illness himself. He was virtually all over the floor. Smith took good shots, went for rebounds, and showed pure versatility. All of which came together in one sequence in the 2nd quarter. At the 7:53 mark, Tre Jones went for the 3-pointer, but missed. Smith grabbed the rebound and kicked it back out to Jones. Jones pumped-faked it before finding the open Buddy Hield on the wing. Hield penetrated the lane, dished it to Smith, who then slammed it down with authority. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) JALEN SMITH IS DOING IT ALL RIGHT NOW! He has 15 first half points 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/xNYLykk9gF — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 23, 2026 He finished the half with 15 points and went 6-for-7 from the field. In Claxton’s absence, Smith has emerged as a major catalyst at center. Altogether, he is averaging 13.4 points and 7.9 rebounds per game while shooting 52.8% from the field. Additionally, Smith has scored in double figures in 11 games this season. His highest-scoring game came on November 11 against the San Antonio Spurs, when he finished with 23 points. Meanwhile, Smith has bounced back from injury scares , usually stemming from aggressive play. Chicago trailed Denver 72-70 at the half. The Bulls will play the Cleveland Cavaliers at home on Monday at 7:00 pm CST/8:00 pm EST. item.title: 34 Years Later, the Best 'Far Side' Quote Will Still Leave You Speechless
item.description: Larson didn’t do deep and inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful . Larson’s work was brilliant, and it sometimes took a few minutes to figure out what the punchline was. Take, this comic strip where an artist is painting a woman as a half-fly creature, for example. You likely see the woman or the painting first, and you wonder why the artist is painting her that way. Only after inspecting the comic more closely do you see the dead fly stuck to his glasses.

item.title: Pierre LeBrun Reveals Stunning Dylan Larkin Trade Secret Kept Quiet for Months
item.description: The Dylan Larkin trade saga finally came to an end Sunday night when the Detroit Red Wings sent their former captain to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster deal. But according to NHL insider Pierre LeBrun , there was a major secret being kept behind the scenes for months. And it changes the way we look at how this entire situation unfolded. Following the trade, LeBrun revealed that Larkin had actually been willing to accept a move to Montreal for more than two months. However, the Canadiens and Larkin’s representatives reportedly agreed to keep that information quiet. “So, it turns out Dylan Larkin was actually open to a trade to Montreal for more than two months,” LeBrun wrote on X, according to the post provided. “But the Canadiens wanted to keep that quiet because they felt it would add an extra layer of noise that might hamper getting a deal done. And Larkin’s camp agreed.” That’s a fascinating revelation considering the months of speculation surrounding Larkin’s approved trade destinations. Oct 26, 2026; Edmonton, Alberta, CAN; Edmonton Oilers defensemen Ryan Shea (6) looks to clear the puck in front of Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin (71) during the second period at Rogers Place. Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Michael Hage Was the Key to Getting the Deal Done According to LeBrun, Montreal had been a legitimate possibility much longer than the public realized. However, the Canadiens still had to satisfy Detroit’s asking price, which reportedly included one particularly important asset. Michael Hage. “Montreal agreeing to include Hage was a huge must for the Red Wings,” LeBrun reported. “The deal started to come together and get serious on Friday.” That detail is especially interesting considering Hage had previously emerged as a potential centerpiece in a hypothetical deal between the two organizations. Now, we know just how important the 20-year-old University of Michigan standout was to Detroit’s negotiations. According to the NHL’s official trade announcement , the Red Wings received Hage, Kirby Dach, Samuel Montembeault, two conditional first-round picks, a second-round selection, and a fourth-round pick. Montreal received Larkin, along with Detroit’s 2027 third-round and 2028 second-round selections. Michael Hage. “Montreal agreeing to include Hage was a huge must for the Red Wings,” LeBrun reported. “The deal started to come together and get serious on Friday.” That detail is especially interesting considering Hage had previously emerged as a potential centerpiece in a hypothetical deal between the two organizations. According to the NHL’s official trade announcement , the Red Wings received Hage, Kirby Dach, Samuel Montembeault, two conditional first-round picks, a second-round selection, and a fourth-round pick. item.title: Penguins Get Goalie’d; Play Well, Lose Anway
item.description: DALLAS — Better. Much better, but still not quite good enough. The Pittsburgh Penguins (7-14-2) played their best game in the last handful of offerings, but still had fewer goals on the scoreboard than their opponent, the Dallas Stars (15-6-2). The hockey term is goalie’d as the Penguins had plenty of good scoring chances, but Dallas goalie Jake Oettinger gobbled them up like leftover stuffing after Thanksgiving, and Dallas beat the Penguins 1-0 at American Airlines Arena. The Penguins were significantly better in the first period. The Penguins outshot Dallas 12-11, and the Penguins earned a few glorious chances. A Tommy Novak chance from along the right goal line ended with a miraculous Jake Oettinger save. From nearly the same spot a couple of minutes later, Justin Brazeau hit the post. Midway through the third period, Avery Hayes had a great rip from the slot that was wired for the top corner, but that shot also met Oettinger’s shoulder pads. Rickard Rakell also had a point-blank chance in the final minute, but the Penguins lost anyway. Penguins goalie Arturs Silovs was also quite good. The goal against was unstoppable, but he stopped everything else, and every high-danger chance Dallas threw at him. Egor Chinakhov was also having a game. In the first period, he created a breakaway and then, with a similar defensive stop at the point, launched himself on a one-on-one. However, in all cases, Oettinger made the save. Interestingly, Sidney Crosby had a couple of later third-period shots. He and Chinakhov led the Penguins with four shots on goal. First-period scoring chances: 15-10 Penguins. Second-period chances: 8-2 Dallas. Third-period: 10-2 Penguins. Oettinger was perfect, stopping all 34 shots. Silovs stopped 22 of 23 before being pulled for the extra attacker. Penguins Goal Cap 1-0 Dallas: In a reversal from recent second-period performances, the Penguins were solid. However, good players make good plays. Dallas center Wyatt Johnston turned Penguins D-man Trevor van Riemsdyk inside out at the blue line, and Joel Kiviranta got inside positioning on Kris Letang at the net front. Letang swatted the puck away in anger, but only after Kiviranta (3) deflected Johnston’s hard pass behind Silovs at 12:44 of the second. item.title: Dylan Larkin traded to Montreal Canadiens for goalie, package of picks
item.description: The divorce between the Detroit Red Wings and disgruntled former captain Dylan Larkin is finally complete. Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff traded Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday, Nov. 22, acquiring forwards Kirby Dach, Michigan Wolverines prospect Michael Hage, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 and a second round pick in 2028 and a fourth-round pick in 2028. Larkin is in Year 4 of an eight-year deal carrying an $8.7 million salary cap hit that is highly favorable in a league where the 2026-27 salary cap ceiling is $104 million. Larkin, 30, signed an eight-year, $69.6 million extension with the Wings on March 1, 2023. DYLAN BUCKS: Larkin tops $1 million forfeited while awaiting Red Wings trade Larkin had two goals and four assists in 10 games for the Wings this season, before leaving the team on Oct. 29. The Wings suspended Larkin without pay that same day , costing him $41,237.11 a day. Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, told reporters, "Dylan’s had enough of the situation." Sunday monrig marked more than $1 million of salary forfeited back to the team. Larkin's final goal in a Wings uniform came Oct. 26, tying the game late in the third period at Edmonton in an eventual thrilling shootout win. He didn't play again. LARKIN LATE TYING GOAL 🚨 Red Wings applying massive pressure with the empty net - Seider finds Raymond who gets it to Larkin for the game tying tally. Detroit sends it to overtime. #LGRW pic.twitter.com/yCVN8muhU7 — Ryan Hana (@RyanHanaWWP) October 27, 2026 Larkin was soundly booed by his hometown fans when he was introduced during opening night Oct. 2 at Little Caesars Arena while out with an upper-body injury sustained in the offseason . Larkin was again booed in his season debut Oct. 6 after missing the season's first two games, but turned jeers to cheers after scoring a goal and being named the game's first star. Montreal fans at Bell Centre chanted "We want Larkin!" on Oct. 10, the most notable away crowd reaction to the saga. News broke on June 4 that Larkin, who had a no-trade clause, had requested a trade after 11 seasons with his hometown Wings. Larkin is from nearby Waterford, attended the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor and had been the Wings' captain until he was stripped of the title after the trade request became public. Larkin has gone 10 years without appearing in the NHL playoffs – the Wings own the NHL's longest playoff drought – and his gold-medal success at the 2026 Milano Olympics likely reminded him how fun it is to win important games. He returned to Detroit from that experience, and watched as a Wings team that had been 10 points inside the playoff picture in late January lost its foothold and dropped out of contention, again. Steve Yzerman, removed as GM in July , said shortly after the season he received a phone call from Larkin's agent informing him Larkin wanted to be traded. A week later, a list of teams Larkin would waive his no-trade clause for was provided

Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff traded Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday, Nov. 22, acquiring forwards Kirby Dach, Michigan Wolverines prospect Michael Hage, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 and a second round pick in 2028 and a fourth-round pick in 2028. Larkin is in Year 4 of an eight-year deal carrying an $8.7 million salary cap hit that is highly favorable in a league where the 2026-27 salary cap ceiling is $104 million. Larkin, 30, signed an eight-year, $69.6 million extension with the Wings on March 1, 2023. DYLAN BUCKS: Larkin tops $1 million forfeited while awaiting Red Wings trade Larkin had two goals and four assists in 10 games for the Wings this season, before leaving the team on Oct. 29. The Wings suspended Larkin without pay that same day , costing him $41,237.11 a day. Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, told reporters, "Dylan’s had enough of the situation." Sunday monrig marked more than $1 million of salary forfeited back to the team. Larkin's final goal in a Wings uniform came Oct. 26, tying the game late in the third period at Edmonton in an eventual thrilling shootout win. He didn't play again. LARKIN LATE TYING GOAL 🚨 Red Wings applying massive pressure with the empty net - Seider finds Raymond who gets it to Larkin for the game tying tally. Detroit sends it to overtime. #LGRW pic.twitter.com/yCVN8muhU7 — Ryan Hana (@RyanHanaWWP) October 27, 2026 Larkin was soundly booed by his hometown fans when he was introduced during opening night Oct. 2 at Little Caesars Arena while out with an upper-body injury sustained in the offseason . Larkin was again booed in his season debut Oct. 6 after missing the season's first two games, but turned jeers to cheers after scoring a goal and being named the game's first star. Montreal fans at Bell Centre chanted "We want Larkin!" on Oct. 10, the most notable away crowd reaction to the saga. News broke on June 4 that Larkin, who had a no-trade clause, had requested a trade after 11 seasons with his hometown Wings. Larkin is from nearby Waterford, attended the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor and had been the Wings' captain until he was stripped of the title after the trade request became public. Larkin has gone 10 years without appearing in the NHL playoffs – the Wings own the NHL's longest playoff drought – and his gold-medal success at the 2026 Milano Olympics likely reminded him how fun it is to win important games. He returned to Detroit from that experience, and watched as a Wings team that had been 10 points inside the playoff picture in late January lost its foothold and dropped out of contention, again. Steve Yzerman, removed as GM in July , said shortly after the season he received a phone call from Larkin's agent informing him Larkin wanted to be traded. A week later, a list of teams Larkin would waive his no-trade clause for was provided. Larkin's initial trade wish list – provided by his agent Brisson, who represented Horcoff during his NHL career in 2000-16 – was limited to three teams: Florida Panthers, Vegas Golden Knights and Minnesota Wild. The Panthers then traded with Ottawa for Brady Tkachuk , taking them out of the Larkin bidding. "Dylan has five years remaining on his contract," Yzerman said June 27 after the NHL Draft. "My job as the manager of the Detroit Red Wings is always to do what is in the best interest of the Detroit Red Wings and I will act accordingly to that. I cannot make any guarantees or did not make any guarantees that that request could or would be met." The list expanded in the fall to 10 teams to include the Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. Horcoff said Sept. 16, one day after being named interim GM, that a rebuild was "out of the question," making the Larkin situation more difficult to resolve. "We have too many good players in that lineup," Horcoff said. "We've been close. The last three years in a row, we've been really close. We're not looking backward, we're looking forward. We want to focus on what it's going to take for us to get over that hump." But a Larkin deal finally came to fruition – while restricted free agent Simon Edvinsson bizarrely remains without a contract and wishes to be traded. (He must sign a contract by the 5 p.m. deadline on Dec. 1 or sit out the season in the NHL.) Larkin now gets a chance to show what he can do elsewhere and return to the playoffs for the first time since 2016, his rookie year, while the Wings work to reshape their roster. The Wings on Oct. 14 signed Alex DeBrincat to a seven-year, $91 million contract extension , the richest deal in franchise history. This breaking news story will be updated. Contact Helene St. James at Hstjames@freepress.com. Read more on the Detroit Red Wings and sign up for our Red Wings newsletter . item.title: 49ers’ Colton McKivitz suffers gruesome injury vs. Vikings
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers have been dealt a devastating injury blow with right tackle Colton McKivitz in the first half of the Week 11 game against the Minnesota Vikings. The injury occurred in the second quarter of the contest and it was immediately clear that the 49ers offensive lineman suffered a gruesome ankle injury. McKivitz came down with the injury when he got his leg trapped under another player. You can check out video of the aftermath of the play in which McKivitz got hurt right here , but warning, it is hard to watch. MORE: DK Metcalf facing suspension after Week 11 ejection vs. Eagles McKivitz stayed down on the field after the play and was tended to by the training staff before being loaded onto a cart and being taken off the field. Players on both teams were obviously very distraught at the site of McKivitz’s gruesome leg injury that is going to keep him out for the rest of the season. The good news is, McKivitz was alert while leaving the field in the cart, but that doesn’t change just how awful it was to see him get injured. MORE: Dak Prescott makes Cowboys history in dominant win over Titans The loss is a tough one for the Niners, as McKivitz is one of the team’s best offensive linemen, and he’s one of the best right tackles in the sport. Entering Week 11, McKivitz was having a phenomenal season with Pro Football Focus grades of 82.8 overall, 71.0 in pass-blocking and 88.8 in run-blocking, ranking seventh, 37th and second among tackles in the NFL. McKivitz didn’t allow a single sack and permitted just 12 pressures in 317 pass-blocking snaps. Vederian Lowe is the next man up for San Francisco, but he will present a significant downgrade for the Niners’ offense. 49ers’ injury woes continue San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan looks on prior to the game against the Miami Dolphins at Levi’s Stadium. Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) No team in the NFL has been as ravaged by injuries as San Francisco this season. Going into the Sunday night game against the Vikings, the 49ers had a whopping 14 players on injured reserve . McKivitz will unfortunately be No. 15. Despite all of their injuries, the Niners have been one of the best teams in the NFL this season. Considering everything the Niners have had to overcome, there’s no question head coach Kyle Shanahan is one of the top candidates for Coach of the Year. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

MORE: DK Metcalf facing suspension after Week 11 ejection vs. Eagles McKivitz stayed down on the field after the play and was tended to by the training staff before being loaded onto a cart and being taken off the field. Players on both teams were obviously very distraught at the site of McKivitz’s gruesome leg injury that is going to keep him out for the rest of the season. The good news is, McKivitz was alert while leaving the field in the cart, but that doesn’t change just how awful it was to see him get injured. MORE: Dak Prescott makes Cowboys history in dominant win over Titans The loss is a tough one for the Niners, as McKivitz is one of the team’s best offensive linemen, and he’s one of the best right tackles in the sport. Entering Week 11, McKivitz was having a phenomenal season with Pro Football Focus grades of 82.8 overall, 71.0 in pass-blocking and 88.8 in run-blocking, ranking seventh, 37th and second among tackles in the NFL. McKivitz didn’t allow a single sack and permitted just 12 pressures in 317 pass-blocking snaps. Vederian Lowe is the next man up for San Francisco, but he will present a significant downgrade for the Niners’ offense. 49ers’ injury woes continue San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan looks on prior to the game against the Miami Dolphins at Levi’s Stadium. Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) No team in the NFL has been as ravaged by injuries as San Francisco this season. Going into the Sunday night game against the Vikings, the 49ers had a whopping 14 players on injured reserve . McKivitz will unfortunately be No. 15. Despite all of their injuries, the Niners have been one of the best teams in the NFL this season. Considering everything the Niners have had to overcome, there’s no question head coach Kyle Shanahan is one of the top candidates for Coach of the Year. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Weekend Warm-up: Did Bayern Munich do the right thing in signing Jamal Musiala and Alphonso Davies to massive deals?

item.content:encoded: (Photo by Marcel Engelbrecht - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is an uncomfortable question hanging over Bayern Munich’s recent contract strategy — did the club make the right investments in Jamal Musiala and Alphonso Davies, or did it allow the fear of losing two exceptional talents to dictate financial decisions that could eventually become difficult to justify? Both players received lucrative, long-term extensions in February 2025. At the time, Bayern Munich vie wed them as essential building blocks for the future. Musiala was arguably the most exciting young attacking talent in German football, while Davies remained one of Eur ope’s most sought-after left-backs. Losing either player, particularly on a free transfer, would have been a significant sporting and financial setback. At the time that each signed, it was reported that neither had a serious suito r. But there was another consideration that could not be ignored — neither player had an entirely clean injury history. Bayern Munich was committing enormous money to two footballers whose availability had already become a recurring concern. That concern has become considerably harder to dismiss since the contracts were signed. The numbers from Transfermarkt provide some perspective on why Bayern Munich’s decision deserves scrutiny. Its seasonal injury-history summaries include both days unavailable and matches missed, althou gh the records also include some non-injury absences, such as illness, quarantine, and fitness-related issues. Jamal Musiala 2026/27: 73 days missed, 3 injuries/ailments, 12 games missed 2025/26: 216 days missed, 3 injuries/ailments, 38 games missed 2024/25: 97 days missed, 3 injuries/ailments, 15 games missed 2023/24: 72 days missed, 6 injuries/ailments, 12 games missed 2022/23: 25 days missed, 4 injuries/ailments, 4 games missed 2021/22: 25 days missed, 4 injuries/ailments, 6 games missed 2020/21: 25 days missed, 2 injuries/ailments, 1 game missed (Injury stats are through November 19th) Musiala’s injury record became increasingly concerning during his final two seasons before the new contract and immediately afterward. A hamstring injury in November 2023, recurring muscle problems, and a torn muscle bundle in April 2025 interrupted his progress. Then came the devastating broken fibula sustained at the Club World Cup in July 2025, which kept him out for 174 days and 31 matches. Alphonso Davies 2026/27: 5 days, 1 injury/ailment, 1 game missed 2025/26: 126 days, 5 injuries/ailments, 24 games missed 2024/25: 254 days, 3 injuries/ailments, 47 games missed 2023/24: 22 days, 1 injury/ailment, 4 games missed 2022/23: 71 days, 4 injuries/ailments, 10 games missed 2021/22: 140 days, 5 injuries/ailments, 27 games missed 2020/21: 47 days, 1 injury/ailment, 9 games missed 2018/19: 29 days, 1 injury/ailment, 8 games missed (Injury stats are through November 19th) Davies’ record is arguably even more concerning in terms of cumulative absences. His 2021/22 season was interrupted by heart-related problems, while his 2024/25 campaign ended with an anterior cruciate ligament tear suffered on international duty . That injury alone cost him 221 days and 39 matches. Davies subsequently experienced additional muscula r problems, making his return to consistent availability another challenge. Injury prone or bad luck? These figures do not mean either player is destined to remain injury-prone. They do, however, demonstrate that Bayern Munich was not unaware of the availability risks when it committed to these contracts. In Davies’s case, the question about investing that much into the left-back position for a player with that kind of injury track record is likely causing a lot of internal Monday-morning quarterbacking. The financial commitment: What is Bayern actually paying? The reported salaries make the debate considerably more interesting. According to Sport Bild , the estimated annual salaries for the two players are listed below: Musiala: More than €25 million per year, including potential bonuses. Per Capology , Musiala’s potential bonuses total €12,450,000. Davies: Up to €20 million per year, including potential bonuses. Per Capology , Davies’ potential bonuses total €5,000,000. Tho se are reported figures, not officially disclosed salaries. There is also a distinction between base salary and performance-related compensation. Capology , which publishes estimated salary data, currently puts Musiala’s gross fixed annual salary at approximately €22.83 million and Davies’s at €15 million, excluding bonuses. As you can see, there are some discrepancies becaus e figures are not publicly released as you might see in North American sports. That distinction between salary and total financial package matters. The headline figures are no t necessarily guaranteed annual payments, and performance incentives can make a significant difference. Some recent salary coverage also suggests Musiala’s maximum compensation is linked to playing-time thresholds. The exact contractual structure has not been officially confirmed. There is another particularly interesting detail from the latest Sport Bild reporting (via @iMiaSanMia ) — both players reportedly negotiated special provisions for continued salary payments during extended injury absences. Musiala’s protection allegedly extends to six months, while Davies’s is reportedly limited to three or four months. Bayern is also said to have taken out additional insurance to mitigate the financial exposure. In other words, Bayern was not simply agreeing to pay two players enormous salaries . It was reportedly agreeing to additional financial protection even if injuries kept them away from the pitch for extended periods. That is a s ubstantial commitment. Why Bayern needed to make the deals There is a very good argument that Bayern could not afford to lose either player in 2025. Mu siala was 21, already a Germany international, and had developed into one of Europe’s most exciting attacking midfielders. He was producin g goals, assists, and moments of individual brilliance while becoming increasingly central to Bayern’s identity. He was also approaching the final year of his previous contract. The danger of allowing a player of that caliber to enter the final year of his deal without an extension was obvious. Premier League and La Liga clubs were interested, and Bayern risked either losing him for nothing or being forced into a s ale on unfavorable terms. The BBC reported that Musial a had been granted a release clause as part of his new agreement, but the overall decision to retain him was understandable. Bayern needed a player around whom it could build its next generation. Davies presented a different but equally difficult situation. At 24, he was an es tablished Champions League winner with extraordinary pace, athleticism, and experience at the highest level. He was also attracting considerable interest from elsewhere, particularly Real Madrid, and was approaching the end of his existing contract. Losing a playe r of his quality without receiving a transfer fee would have been a significant blow. Finding a comparable replacement would also have req uired a substantial investment. Bayern Munich ultimately secured both players through 2030. That gave the club long-term security, protected the value of two important assets, and avoided the possibility of watching them leave for nothing. There was also a symbolic component. Bayern w anted to demonstrate that it could compete financially with Europe’s wealthiest clubs and retain its most valuable young players. Letting Musiala or Davies w alk would have sent precisely the wrong message. Where Bayern might have made a mistake The strongest arg ument against the contracts is not that Musiala and Davies were undeserving of significant pay raises. Both had demonstrated their value. It is that Bayern may have negotiated as though retaining them was more important than protecti

item.title: Fed-up Cal Bears fans curse out players after Stanford rout in Big Game
item.description: Some Cal football fans have had enough. Following the Golden Bears’ rough 44-28 loss in the “Big Game” to their cross-bay rivals Stanford, falling to 3-8 on the season, fans were caught on video cursing out players as they left the field. It’s never good when opposing fans rush the field in your home stadium. But that’s not an excuse for fans cussing out college football players and putting it on the internet. California Golden Bears head coach Tosh Lupoi looks on against the Stanford Cardinal in Berkeley, Calif., Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Getty Images But that’s where the Golden Bears find themselves while head coach Tosh Lupoi faces real questions about his job security as an embarrassing season winds down. But Cal hasn’t been competitive for over a month. They haven’t won since knocking off Virginia Tech on Oct. 10, and have lost by an average of 26.2 points over their ongoing five-game losing streak. They’ll look to snap it in their season finale next week when they host Pittsburgh. Virginia head coach Tony Elliott, left, shakes hands with California head coach Tosh Lupoi after a game at Scott Stadium in Charlottesville, Va., Nov. 14, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cal fans are not happy pic.twitter.com/Okjhl1kiUi — Stuckey (@Stuckey2) November 22, 2026 Lupoi signed a five-year, $22.6 million contract that was finalized in early October, meaning moving on would require Cal to take on a hefty buyout while the school faces a serious budget crisis. Cal’s athletic program reportedly came into the season facing a $24 million deficit and laid off some 20 people in the marketing, athletic communications and creative services departments. Stanford Cardinal players celebrate with the Stanford Axe after defeating the California Golden Bears, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Berkeley, Calif. Getty Images All while costs have risen during the transition to the Atlantic Coast Conference following the dismantling of the Pac-12 in 2024. Suffice to say, barring something drastic and unforeseen, the feeling coming out of Saturday’s loss to Stanford won’t dissipate anytime soon.

item.title: Red Wings Deal The MN Wild Trade Target to Canada
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dylan Larkin hasn’t played a game for the Detroit Red Wings since Oct. 26 against Edmonton. But the Minnesota Wild have been chasing him since the 30-year-old center asked for a trade going all the way back to June. In fact, Minnesota was on his original three-team trade list, and the only team league-wide that stayed in it from start to finish. Unfortunately, all that effort went for naught on Sunday evening when news broke that the Team USA Olympic gold medalist has finally accepted a trade to the one place he’s been trying to avoid for months. Red Wings trade Dylan Larkin to Montreal, not the MN Wild Dylan Larkin has been traded to the Montreal Canadiens for two players, a prospect’s rights and four draft picks. Larkin accepted his fate after forfeiting more than $1 million in salary due to suspension. The Canadiens have acquired forward Dylan Larkin, Detroit’s second-round pick in 2028 and third-round pick in 2027 in exchange for forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, the rights to forward Michael Hage, a first-round pick in 2027, a second-round pick in 2027, a fourth-round pick in 2028 and a first-round pick in 2029. #GoHabsGo — Canadiens Montréal (@CanadiensMTL) November 22, 2026 Both teams announced the trade around 7:45 p.m. Central. Detroit gets forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault and the rights to prospect Michael Hage, plus first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick. Montreal also gets Detroit’s second-round pick in 2028 and third-round pick in 2027. Neither team announced any retained salary. Related: Reports: Injury to MN Wild Superstar Not Considered Serious David Pagnotta ( The Fourth Period ) said Sunday night that the Canadiens had started warming up to moving Hage a few weeks ago, but Larkin wouldn’t waive for Montreal at the time. Michael Russo ( The Athletic ) said a Wild source had already told him the Canadiens would get Larkin by the end of the week. There ya go. Wild source said the other day Habs would get him by end of week. Larkin couldn’t sit out forever https://t.co/SndgY54obZ — Michael Russo (@RussoHockey) November 22, 2026 What Montreal gets in Dylan Larkin Obviously, the Minnesota Wild have proven early this season (with a 17-3-5 start) that they do not need Dylan Larkin to win hockey games. However, you can bet Bill Guerin will be on the phone this week trying to devise a plan to get the Central Division leader over the top, come playoffs. Meanwhile, Montreal gets a center who led Detroit’s forwards in average ice time at 21:41 this season, with 2 goals, 4 assists and a plus-3 in 10 games. item.title: Coaches Poll Delivers Encouraging Sign for SEC Ahead of Rivalry Week
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; Georgia Bulldogs running back Nate Frazier (3) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the first half against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) ATHENS, Ga. — College football’s coaches have weighed in, and their latest rankings provide another encouraging development for the Southeastern Conference. Georgia maintained the No. 1 position in Sunday’s US LBM Coaches Poll following its 34-6 victory over South Carolina. However, the Bulldogs were hardly the only SEC program making noise. Alabama, Texas and Tennessee climbed in the rankings, while Oklahoma and Missouri returned to the top 25. As a result, nine SEC teams enter Rivalry Week ranked by the coaches. Georgia remains the standard Georgia (10-1) received 60 first-place votes, keeping the Bulldogs ahead of undefeated Utah and one-loss Notre Dame. The Bulldogs have now won four consecutive games, including decisive victories over Ole Miss, Missouri and South Carolina. Meanwhile, Alabama climbed from No. 7 to No. 5, Texas advanced from No. 8 to No. 6 and Tennessee moved from No. 9 to No. 7. Those improvements matter as the conference prepares to determine Georgia’s opponent in Atlanta. Although the coaches poll does not control playoff selections, the rankings reflect the national perception of teams entering the regular season’s final stretch. Complete Coaches Poll Top 25 Rank Team 1 Georgia 2 Utah 3 Notre Dame 4 Miami 5 Alabama 6 Texas 7 Tennessee 8 Wake Forest 9 Texas Tech 10 UCLA 11 BYU 12 Indiana 13 Iowa 14 Oregon 15 USC 16 Arizona 17 Houston 18 Louisville 19 Ole Miss 20 Florida 21 Boise State 22 Oklahoma 23 Missouri 24 Liberty 25 Kentucky One notable difference separates the polls The coaches ranked Alabama fifth, one position ahead of Texas. The AP poll reversed that order, placing Texas fifth and Alabama sixth. Additionally, Kentucky remained in the coaches poll at No. 25 despite dropping out of the AP rankings. Ohio State experienced the opposite situation, falling out of the coaches poll while remaining No. 25 in the AP Top 25. These differences demonstrate how closely voters are evaluating programs with similar records. More importantly, the SEC’s leading teams still have opportunities to influence their postseason positions. Alabama hosts Auburn in the Iron Bowl, Texas visits Texas A&M and Tennessee travels to Vanderbilt. Meanwhile, Georgia closes its regular season against Georgia Tech. The coaches have delivered their latest assessment. Now, the SEC’s biggest rivals get the opportunity to answer on the field. item.title: Red Wings trade ex-captain Dylan Larkin to Canadiens in multiplayer and draft-pick deal
item.description: CALGARY, CANADA - OCTOBER 24: Dylan Larkin #71 of the Detroit Red Wings skates against the Calgary Flames during the second period at the Scotiabank Saddledome on October 24, 2026 in Calgary, Canada. (Photo by Brett Holmes/Getty Images) Getty Images DETROIT — The Detroit Red Wings traded ex-captain Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster swap involving four players and six draft picks, including two first-round selections, in a deal announced by both teams on Sunday night. In acquiring Larkin, the Red Wings landed forward Kirby Dach, goalie Sam Montembeault and prospect forward Michael Hage as well as Montreal’s first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, plus a 2028 second-round selection and a 2028 fourth-rounder. Along with Larkin, Montreal acquired Detroit’s 2028 second-round pick and a third-round selection in 2027. The long-awaited trade happened between two Atlantic Division rivals and a month after the Red Wings suspended Larkin without pay. The suspension came after the player’s agent informed the team the center would no longer play for the franchise, and had grown frustrated by the Red Wings’ inability to move him months after he asked to be dealt. AP Hockey Writer John Wawrow contributed.

item.title: Let fans dream: we're happy, but chasing our dream - Gabriel Milito
item.description: Let fans dream: we're happy, but chasing our dream - Gabriel Milito Chivas put the icing on the cake of their Apertura 2026 regular season: they beat Cruz Azul, seized first place overall with 33 points, finished with the tournament’s best home record, and now await their quarterfinal series against Pachuca. The support of the Red-and-White Nation was crucial to securing their sixth home win, as the Chivas faithful never stopped cheering on Guadalajara for a single second. To overcome La Máquina, the Flock showed the solidity they aim to replicate in their first playoff tie, as Gabriel Milito noted in his post-match press conference. The Chivas coach encouraged the Red-and-White Republic to dream alongside the team as they pursue their ultimate goal. “We finished the regular season very well, winning and taking the opportunity to finish top, which is what we wanted. A new tournament begins, and we all start from zero.” “We have a tough series against Pachuca, a good team. We’ll stay humble as always, looking to compete and play our game, as the team has been doing for some time.” “In these kinds of matches, a bad 10–15 minutes can put your chances of advancing at risk; we’ll try to get as close to perfection as possible. We have to work hard and earn our place in the next round.” “It’s important to have that sense of belonging to the club, as this squad does. Those of us who arrived later are all proud to represent Chivas , and our goal is very clear.” “We know achieving that ultimate goal is no easy task, but we have to keep the dream alive and see how far we can go. Now we have to think solely and exclusively about Pachuca. Today was good; finishing first deserves a lot of credit given everything we went through during the season.” “Hopefully, we can be at our very best for what comes next, which is decisive. The series will demand that of us. The players know how important it is to push ourselves to our limits, both individually and collectively.” “It was important because it was the end of the regular season, and victory would give us not just three points but first place.
