item.content:encoded: Let fans dream: we're happy, but chasing our dream - Gabriel Milito Chivas put the icing on the cake of their Apertura 2026 regular season: they beat Cruz Azul, seized first place overall with 33 points, finished with the tournament’s best home record, and now await their quarterfinal series against Pachuca. The support of the Red-and-White Nation was crucial to securing their sixth home win, as the Chivas faithful never stopped cheering on Guadalajara for a single second. To overcome La Máquina, the Flock showed the solidity they aim to replicate in their first playoff tie, as Gabriel Milito noted in his post-match press conference. The Chivas coach encouraged the Red-and-White Republic to dream alongside the team as they pursue their ultimate goal. “We finished the regular season very well, winning and taking the opportunity to finish top, which is what we wanted. A new tournament begins, and we all start from zero.” “We have a tough series against Pachuca, a good team. We’ll stay humble as always, looking to compete and play our game, as the team has been doing for some time.” “In these kinds of matches, a bad 10–15 minutes can put your chances of advancing at risk; we’ll try to get as close to perfection as possible. We have to work hard and earn our place in the next round.” “It’s important to have that sense of belonging to the club, as this squad does. Those of us who arrived later are all proud to represent Chivas , and our goal is very clear.” “We know achieving that ultimate goal is no easy task, but we have to keep the dream alive and see how far we can go. Now we have to think solely and exclusively about Pachuca. Today was good; finishing first deserves a lot of credit given everything we went through during the season.” “Hopefully, we can be at our very best for what comes next, which is decisive. The series will demand that of us. The players know how important it is to push ourselves to our limits, both individually and collectively.” “It was important because it was the end of the regular season, and victory would give us not just three points but first place. Now a new tournament begins with no clear favorite; that will have to be proven once each match gets underway.” “We’re happy, but we haven’t achieved what we’re striving for.” “Let the fans dream. They’ll keep supporting the team because they see that we give everything, and we bring that competitive spirit we already have to every match. We have to dream. We’re going into this series to let our performances show what we’re capable of.” “Without humility, effort, and the right mentality, you achieve nothing in football. Those are our values, but we have to put them into practice. It will be a difficult series, but one thing is guaranteed: we’ll give it absolutely everything.” “It’s important to finish with the best defensive record and more points than everyone else. If there’s one thing we’ve talked about, it’s being solid and clinical. That’s the ideal combination, and we’ll try to achieve it in these playoffs.” “There are no easy matches in the Mexican league; we’ve seen that many times. We don’t want any surprises. We have to stay focused, which is why I spoke about the team’s maturity and the impression we’re giving.” This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The early games of Week 11 are winding down. It wasn’t the prettiest slate of games, but football games and stats were produced on a field with grass or some kind of turf covering that field. We’ve seen some ugly football today, but as teams lose players to injuries and start young players for evaluation, things get ugly. Week 12 Byes None Week 12 Waiver Wire Pickups Late game update Fernando Mendoza, Raiders, QB (18%) Mendoza complete under 50% of his passes against the Broncos in Denver, but he also put up 267 yards three touchdowns and a pick-six to end the game. Three touchdown passes is pretty good, especially when you consider that Brock Bowers was unable to play. How useful he’ll be in fantasy moving forward is hard to know, but he’s proving he can put up fantasy points with some average receivers. Getting Bowers back will be huge and having Ashton Jeanty breaking off huge catch and runs doesn’t hurt either. Geno Smith, QB, Jets (18%) Smith completed 17-of-21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday’s 27-24 win over the Chargers. He remains a streaming option at quarterback despite inconsistency. Next week he faces the Dolphins, who he put up 287 yards and three touchdowns against in Week 7. Chimere Dike, WR, Tennessee Titans (13%) Dike took over the slot role in Week 11 and ended up leading the team in receptions and yards, catching 6-of-7 targets for 69 yards. It wasn’t a huge fantasy game, but if he can keep that slot job, he should be set up for a good PPR floor moving forward. Jack Bech, Raiders, WR (1%) Fernando Mendoza appears to like wide receiver Jack Bech, as he’s targeted him on 25% of his passes through his first two games. This week Bech caught 8-of-9 targets for88 yards and a touchdown. This usage comes with Brock Bowers off the field for most of the time, but I do like that Mendoza likes him and if that keeps up next week with Bowers possibly back, we may be onto something. Jacoby Brissett, QB, Ravens (21%) Justice Hill, RB, Ravens (21%) With Jacoby Brissett in as the Ravens quarterback, they are going to chuck the ball to finish out the season. In his two starts he’s thrown the ball 49 and 37 times. This isn’t your Lamar Jackson Ravens anymore, as he attempted 20, 20, 31, and 25 passes in his four full starts this year. Derrick Henry needs the threat of Jackson taking off as a runner to keep teams honest. Without that the Ravens aren’t going to force the run like they once did. More passing is great for Zay Flowers and good for Brissett and running back Justice Hill. This week against the Panthers, Brissett completed 24-of-37 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while running twice for seven yards. That’s not winning your league for you, but there is no-doubt upside there if you need help at QB. Derrick Henry had a good game against the Panthers, rushing 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown, while catching four passes for 17 yards. Unfortunately he lost a fumble after one of those receptions and he appeared to have suffered a concussion late in the game on his 15-yard touchdown run. That could set up more touches for passing down back Hill next week against the Texans. This week he played well, rushing six times for 69 yards and a touchdown, while catching 4-of-5 targets for 27 yards. He also lost a fumble in the back of the end zone. He was so close to two touchdowns on the day. Even if Henry doesn’t miss time, Hill is worth a pickup in this more pass oriented offense moving forward. Ted Hurst, WR, Buccaneers (1%) Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers were finally forced to throw the ball, and it didn’t go great, as they lost to the Lions, but that was likely. The good news is that Mayfield and company were able to put up some fantasy points through the air. The leader of the group ended up being Hurst, who led the team in targets, receptions, yards and touchdowns. He caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards and a pair of touchdowns. We’ve seen Hurst show out in the past, but this looks like we could see him take over as WR1 if he can stay healthy. The Bucs really need someone to step up in the receiving game, and I like Hurst’s chances. Caleb Douglas, WR, Dolphins (46%) Kyle McCord is not good. But, he is still targeting Douglas like a No. 1 wide receiver. This week he threw in his general direction 10 times, but only completed two passes for 30 yards to the rookie. The looks are there, but the connection isn’t. Next week the Dolphins get the Jets, who Douglas caught two touchdowns against last time they met in Week 7. If you are in a matchup next week that doesn’t look good for your team, get Douglas into your lineup for a shot at some offensive fireworks.

item.title: Urban Meyer Puts Ryan Day’s Ohio State on Alert With Blunt Michigan Warning: “That Concerns Me”
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN – SEPTEMBER 05: Former college football coach and Fox Sports announcer Urban Meyer watches the Indiana Hoosiers play against the North Texas Mean Green on September 5, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) ©Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Urban Meyer just fired a warning shot at Ryan Day ahead of Ohio State’s rivalry showdown with Michigan. The Buckeyes (7–4) are reeling from a humiliating 31–28 loss to Nebraska, while Michigan (6–5) is riding high after stunning previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA, 18–16, in triple overtime. With “The Game” looming in Columbus, Meyer delivered a brutal assessment of what awaits Ohio State on Saturday. Speaking on a recent appearance shared by Eleven Warriors, the three-time national champion coach didn’t hold back on either side of the rivalry. While he flat-out ripped Michigan’s sluggish offense as the worst in college football, he warned Ohio State that defensive coordinator Jay Hill’s unit is more than good enough to drag the Buckeyes into an ugly dogfight. “I think the Wolverine defense is legit, legit, because that offense is pathetic up there,” Meyer said . “And we covered them on Big Noon a bunch. And their defense, what they did to UCLA, was absolutely phenomenal.” Even though Meyer believes Ohio State has the better overall roster, he admitted that Michigan’s defense is outperforming every single unit, offense, defense, or special teams, on either side right now. Urban Meyer's stark assessment of Ohio State's vulnerability is a red flag Ryan Day can't ignore. item.content:encoded: BLOOMINGTON, IN – SEPTEMBER 05: Former college football coach and Fox Sports announcer Urban Meyer watches the Indiana Hoosiers play against the North Texas Mean Green on September 5, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) ©Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Urban Meyer just fired a warning shot at Ryan Day ahead of Ohio State’s rivalry showdown with Michigan. The Buckeyes (7–4) are reeling from a humiliating 31–28 loss to Nebraska, while Michigan (6–5) is riding high after stunning previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA, 18–16, in triple overtime. With “The Game” looming in Columbus, Meyer delivered a brutal assessment of what awaits Ohio State on Saturday. Speaking on a recent appearance shared by Eleven Warriors, the three-time national champion coach didn’t hold back on either side of the rivalry. While he flat-out ripped Michigan’s sluggish offense as the worst in college football, he warned Ohio State that defensive coordinator Jay Hill’s unit is more than good enough to drag the Buckeyes into an ugly dogfight. “I think the Wolverine defense is legit, legit, because that offense is pathetic up there,” Meyer said . “And we covered them on Big Noon a bunch. And their defense, what they did to UCLA, was absolutely phenomenal.” Even though Meyer believes Ohio State has the better overall roster, he admitted that Michigan’s defense is outperforming every single unit, offense, defense, or special teams, on either side right now. Urban Meyer's stark assessment of Ohio State's vulnerability is a red flag Ryan Day can't ignore. Subscribe to stay ahead of the biggest developments in college football's most heated rivalry. “The best unit performing right now is a Wolverine defense, and that concerns me a little bit,” Meyer admitted, pointing out that only one team all year (Oregon) has managed to score more than 21 points on them and that they held a 10–0 UCLA squad to just three points until late in regulation before winning in triple overtime. Looking closely at Michigan’s roller-coaster 2026 campaign under first-year head coach Kyle Whittingham, it is easy to see why Meyer is losing sleep over that side of the ball. Despite an offense that scored just six points in losses to both Indiana and Michigan State, and saw offensive coordinator Jason Beck get fired mid-season, Hill’s defense has carried the entire program on its back. Against UCLA on Saturday night, the Wolverines forced three turnovers, racked up four sacks, and stuffed the Bruins in triple overtime to clinch bowl eligibility, proving they can suffocate even top-five offenses when the game is on the line. That dominant defensive identity is exactly why Meyer sounded worried when he turned his attention directly to his former program. “Our offense has been up and down a little bit, and now we’re down to our backup quarterback. So I see this being a very low-scoring game. This is Ohio State-Wolverine football. The toughest team is going to win this game,” Meyer said. Even though Meyer praised wide receiver Jeremiah Smith as the best player in the country, and maybe the best player ever to play college football, he noted that Ohio State’s shaky offensive line and backup quarterback situation will turn Saturday into a pure rock fight where whoever punches hardest wins. Still, Meyer predicted a tight 17–10 or 17–14 finish and gave the narrow edge to the Buckeyes. The stats from Saturday’s collapse in Lincoln back up every word of Meyer’s concern about Ohio State’s front line and defense. While Smith put on another historic show, catching six passes for 165 yards and two touchdowns to tie Terry Glenn’s single-season school record with 17 touchdown grabs, and freshman Luke Fahey threw for 259 yards in relief of injured starter Julian Sayin, Ohio State’s offensive line got pushed around for just 76 rushing yards. Meanwhile, the Buckeye defense gave up 176 rushing yards and allowed Nebraska to convert 10 of 16 third downs and both fourth-down tries as the Huskers snapped a 31-game losing streak against AP Top 25 teams. For Ryan Day, hearing Meyer bring up the word “toughness” ahead of the Michigan game always hits a sensitive nerve, especially with both coaches facing plenty of heat from their respective fanbases after underwhelming regular seasons. While Ohio State snapped a four-game losing streak in the rivalry with a 27–9 victory in Ann Arbor last November to improve Day’s career record against the Wolverines to 2–4, Michigan has still won the last two meetings inside Ohio Stadium, including a bruising 13–10 defensive rock fight in Columbus in 2024 that looked almost identical to the low-scoring slugfest Meyer is predicting next weekend. With both teams sitting outside the 12-team playoff bracket and pride squarely on the line, Saturday’s clash will come down to which team dominates the trenches when everything goes wrong . item.title: Player grades: SGA-less Thunder punt in 123-113 loss to Heat
item.description: Eventually scratched from his first game of the season, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's absence turned this into a skippable watch at worst and background noise at best. The two-time MVP winner went through his pregame warmups, but that was it in his sole visit to one of the most historic gyms in the NBA. The Oklahoma City Thunder stomached through a 123-113 loss to the Miami Heat . They trailed the entire night and by as many as 20 points. Before the cross-conference matchup even happened, the Thunder punted it on the front end of road back-to-back. Not only was Gilgeous-Alexander, but so were Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Cason Wallace, Alex Caruso and plenty of other names. To twist the knife, Aday Mara was a very-late scratch, too. Sure, the Heat were without Giannis Antetokounmpo, but it was a matchup of their B squad butting heads with OKC's C squad. The only Opening Night starter who was suited up for the Thunder was Isaiah Hartenstein. This is the NBA reality they're in right now with their long list of injuries. Any hopes of a miraculous win popped like a balloon. Not even three minutes in, the Thunder were in an 11-2 deficit. Klay Thompson grilled them from the outside — ala 2016. Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain tried their best collective carry job, but just didn't have the scoring superpowers to do so. The Thunder were in a 36-24 deficit after the first quarter. Finally, the Thunder enjoyed some outside shooting luck. Kenrich Williams drained a 3-pointer to make it a single-digit contest. But anytime it felt like OKC was about to go on a run, the Heat answered back with timely outside jumpers. That was the game's flow throughout the first half. The Thunder had 30 points in the second quarter. They entered halftime with a 67-54 deficit. Bam Adebayo balled out as he flirted with a triple-double. It was the first time this year that he enjoyed first-option hoops. Alas, the second half brought zero intrigue. It was mostly the same as both teams played it out of necessity. Williams had some nice scoring plays, but made costly mistakes as he was asked to be one of their top players. Josh Dix also showed flashes as OKC's best two-way guy with outside makes and good defensive energy. Mitchell had an epic four-point play. But yeah, that's really it. We're really grasping at straws to find meaty thoughts on this inevitable loss once Gilgeous-Alexander was ruled out. The Thunder had 26 points in the third quarter, but the Heat continued to stiff-arm them on the scoreboard. At that juncture in the game, OKC was in a 95-80 hole. Remember when it had a several-year run as one of the league's top defenses? If you stayed through this, you're a real NBA trooper. Enjoy whatever online brownie points you can get. The skeleton Thunder gave you every incentive to tune into the NFL Sunday slate instead. The fourth quarter was forgettable as the game got out of hand. OKC put up 33 points in the final frame to pretty up the final score of this wire-to-wire defeat.

The Oklahoma City Thunder stomached through a 123-113 loss to the Miami Heat . They trailed the entire night and by as many as 20 points. Before the cross-conference matchup even happened, the Thunder punted it on the front end of road back-to-back. Not only was Gilgeous-Alexander, but so were Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Cason Wallace, Alex Caruso and plenty of other names. To twist the knife, Aday Mara was a very-late scratch, too. Sure, the Heat were without Giannis Antetokounmpo, but it was a matchup of their B squad butting heads with OKC's C squad. The only Opening Night starter who was suited up for the Thunder was Isaiah Hartenstein. This is the NBA reality they're in right now with their long list of injuries. Any hopes of a miraculous win popped like a balloon. Not even three minutes in, the Thunder were in an 11-2 deficit. Klay Thompson grilled them from the outside — ala 2016. Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain tried their best collective carry job, but just didn't have the scoring superpowers to do so. The Thunder were in a 36-24 deficit after the first quarter. Finally, the Thunder enjoyed some outside shooting luck. Kenrich Williams drained a 3-pointer to make it a single-digit contest. But anytime it felt like OKC was about to go on a run, the Heat answered back with timely outside jumpers. That was the game's flow throughout the first half. The Thunder had 30 points in the second quarter. They entered halftime with a 67-54 deficit. Bam Adebayo balled out as he flirted with a triple-double. It was the first time this year that he enjoyed first-option hoops. Alas, the second half brought zero intrigue. It was mostly the same as both teams played it out of necessity. Williams had some nice scoring plays, but made costly mistakes as he was asked to be one of their top players. Josh Dix also showed flashes as OKC's best two-way guy with outside makes and good defensive energy. Mitchell had an epic four-point play. But yeah, that's really it. We're really grasping at straws to find meaty thoughts on this inevitable loss once Gilgeous-Alexander was ruled out. The Thunder had 26 points in the third quarter, but the Heat continued to stiff-arm them on the scoreboard. At that juncture in the game, OKC was in a 95-80 hole. Remember when it had a several-year run as one of the league's top defenses? If you stayed through this, you're a real NBA trooper. Enjoy whatever online brownie points you can get. The skeleton Thunder gave you every incentive to tune into the NFL Sunday slate instead. The fourth quarter was forgettable as the game got out of hand. OKC put up 33 points in the final frame to pretty up the final score of this wire-to-wire defeat. The Thunder shot 46% from the field and went 16-of-35 (45.7%) from 3. They shot 13-of-19 on free throws. They had 24 assists on 42 baskets. Six Thunder players scored double-digit points. Mitchell had 17 points and three assists. McCain finished with 20 points and three assists. Williams tallied 12 points and four rebounds. Bennett Stirtz had a career-best 21 points and five assists. Dix had 13 points and five rebounds. Nique Clifford had 11 points and three rebounds. Meanwhile, the Heat shot 53% from the field and went 15-of-38 (39.5%) from 3. They shot 18-of-21 on free throws. They had 30 assists on 45 baskets. Seven Heat players scored double-digit points. Adebayo led the way with a 24-point, 15-rebound and 12-assist triple-double. Pelle Larsson had 21 points and five assists. Nikola Jovic finished with 15 points and eight rebounds. Davion Mitchell tallied 14 points and four rebounds. Bobby Portis Jr. had 10 points and eight rebounds. Ryan Conwell scored 10 points. Simone Fontecchio scored 11 points. Well, not much to say about this one. It was over as soon as the Thunder ruled out most of their main rotation. I can't believe this is OKC's reality. Just an absolute doomsday scenario. I can feel the fanbase becoming numb to it, so I just wanted to remind folks how surreal this last month has been. Mitchell and McCain have been helpful, but it's clear they're just not guys who can carry for an entire game. You take this punch on the chin and move on. The Thunder punted this one. I guess the good news is that it happened against an Eastern Conference foe, so the NBA standings and tie-breaking scenarios aren't as consequential. Just get to New Year's. That's all you need to whisper to yourself to cope a little. Because this has just been a brutal stretch of bad basketball from a group that made winning 60-plus look like a walk in the park. Let's look at Thunder player grades: Ajay Mitchell: C-minus Getting the ball at the top of the key, Mitchell went up for the outside jumper. He splashed it in as Conwell invaded his landing space. The four-point play was one of the rare highlights of a forgettable second half. Sadly, the 24-year-old is showing signs of wear and tear recently. Mitchell finished with 17 points on 6-of-17 shooting, three assists and three rebounds. He shot 2-of-3 from 3 and went 3-of-5 on free throws. He also had two steals. As the Southern saying goes — bless your heart. The Thunder have loaded responsibilities on top of responsibilities. To the point that Mitchell is dropping food off his plate. It's just too much to reasonably expect from your projected Sixth Man to be the top scorer on any given night. He tried his best with 11 points in the first half. But was schemed out of the second half as the game got out of hand. A lot fell on Mitchell's shoulders. He tried to muscle his way to the paint. But to little avail. The jumper was also wishy-washy. He learned what life is like for your average top NBA scoring option. If we're being real here, the Thunder had no shot of generating enough offense to get the shocking upset. They just have way too much talent sidelined right now. After a hot start as OKC's impromptu Robin, Mitchell has crashed back down to Earth in recent weeks. It's turning out to be too much of a burden to carry. Which is understandable for the 24-year-old. Just a shame that he had such a golden opportunity in front of him to skyrocket his way into top-young-player-in-league talks. Just to struggle with the brute workload associated with that. Good defense ➡️ great offense pic.twitter.com/8Kj3TUFon0 — OKC THUNDER (@okcthunder) November 22, 2026 Grab and go 🚦 pic.twitter.com/hEF750HLjy — OKC THUNDER (@okcthunder) November 22, 2026 Splash 💦 pic.twitter.com/UjrY3L7xAS — OKC THUNDER (@okcthunder) November 23, 2026 Jared McCain: C-plus On a scramble second-chance look, the Thunder ping-ponged the ball around the perimeter. In one of their halfcourt offensive possessions, Mitchell launched a pass to McCain. He drilled the corner 3-pointer. His outside jumper was one of their rare sources of offense. McCain finished with 20 points on 7-of-17 shooting, three assists and two rebounds. He shot 2-of-7 from 3 and went 4-of-5 on free throws. Considering that practically every shot attempt was up for grabs, McCain gladly filled in the vacuum. The 22-year-old has never been gun-shy. It's one of his best qualities as a microwave scorer. Alongside Mitchell, those two helped the Thunder stay within reach in a competitive first half. The second half saw him hunkered down as a scorer. Considering the circumstances, McCain had the green light to be a nuanced scorer. Not just a catch-and-shoot guy. He sliced through Miami's defense. He also hunted some mid-range looks. His stubborness to go inside the paint also helped him get to the free-throw line. He had 13 points in a super-active first half. Once he cooled off, the Thunder were ran out of the gym. Just like

item.title: COP31: Onuigbo tasks legislators on climate laws, funding
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The President of GLOBE Legislators International, Rt. Hon. Sir Sam Ifeanyi Onuigbo, has urged parliamentarians across the world to translate international climate agreements into enforceable national laws, backed by adequate funding and effective oversight. Onuigbo said international climate agreements would achieve little unless national parliaments incorporated decisions reached at United Nations climate conferences into domestic legislation and ensured their implementation. He made the call at the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) COP31 Parliamentary Meeting in Antalya, Türkiye, where he highlighted the role of legislators in ensuring that commitments reached at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Conferences of the Parties (COPs) produced tangible results at the national level. In a statement made available to journalists in Gombe on Saturday, the former member of the House of Representatives said parliamentarians must deploy their constitutional powers of lawmaking, budgetary appropriation and oversight to ensure governments implement international climate commitments. Drawing on his legislative experience, Onuigbo recalled that his participation in the GLOBE COP21 Legislators Summit in Paris influenced his decision to sponsor Nigeria’s Climate Change Act. He argued that without the necessary legislative backing, negotiations and agreements reached at international climate conferences could fail to translate into practical outcomes. “After all the contributions here, if they are not brought down into laws for implementation, it becomes an exercise in futility,” he said. Onuigbo described parliamentary action as central to bridging the gap between international climate negotiations and domestic implementation. He stressed that legislators must ensure that agreements reached at COP meetings were reflected in national laws, budgetary allocations and effective government oversight. Describing the deliberations at the Antalya meeting as detailed and incisive, he said their impact would ultimately depend on the ability of parliamentarians to translate the discussions into actionable legislation. The GLOBE Legislators president also commended the National Council on Climate Change, its leadership under Dr Majekodunmi, researchers and other stakeholders for their contributions to the development of the Host Country Approval Criteria for Carbon Market Activities in Nigeria and the country’s broader climate change efforts. He also acknowledged President Bola Tinubu’s role in Nigeria’s climate change efforts. “Above all, I want to thank President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who has exercised admirable leadership in ensuring that the climate journey remains steady and very successful,” he said. Onuigbo was inaugurated as President of GLOBE Legislators at the United Kingdom Parliament on June 24, 2026. Established in 1991, GLOBE Legislators works to strengthen parliamentary engagement and international cooperatio

item.title: $1 of GPT-5.1 tokens finds new ways around China’s Great Firewall
item.description: Researchers have found new ways to evade China’s Great Firewall after spending just $1 worth of tokens. That result appeared last week in a paper titled “CircumVolve: Automated Discovery of Censorship Evasion Strategies Using Large Language Models” presented at the Conference on Computer and Communications Security run by the Association for Computing Machinery’s Special Interest Group on Security, Audit and Control. Penned by six researchers from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Colorado Boulder, and activist group the Great Firewall Report, the paper points out that finding holes in the Great Firewall is a laborious process – so just the kind of task worth handing to AI. The authors came up with a tool they call “CircumVolve” and describe as “a system for automated discovery of censorship circumvention strategies across the full network stack.” “CircumVolve combines LLM code generation with iterative feedback-driven evaluation to produce verifiable and deployable evasion techniques,” they wrote. “CircumVolve models different censorship techniques as discrete scenarios, each capturing the specific context, protocol constraints, and blocking mechanisms of real-world censors. Within each scenario, evasion strategies are represented as executable Python programs that implement packet and protocol manipulations — from rewriting TCP/IP header fields, to crafting DNS queries that exploit parser ambiguities, to modifying the internal structure of encrypted QUIC Initial packets — while maintaining protocol correctness within tolerable bounds or strategically violating it when beneficial.” The authors tested CircumVolve on simulated censorship tools used by China, Iran, Pakistan, and Kazakhstan, and on virtual private servers deployed on clouds in those countries. Those tests found the median API cost to the first successful evasion was less than $1 in token expenditure costs when using GPT-5.1. The authors acknowledge that operators of censorship infrastructure might be able to observe CircumVolve at work, but feel its relatively small payloads – 80 KB of outgoing and 150 KB of incoming traffic – and 25-45-second pauses between tests might see it fly under the radar. “CircumVolve represents a first step in leveraging LLMs to accelerate the censorship-circumvention lifecycle,” the authors wrote. “By automating the labor-intensive tasks of protocol analysis, implementation, and testing, AI-driven approaches make studying circumvention capabilities far more accessible to the comparatively under-resourced Internet freedom community [and] demonstrates how AI-assisted systems can narrow the resource gap between Internet freedom advocates and well-funded censoring states.” Lenovo finally cracks monster datacenter profits Ever since acquiring IBM’s x86 server business in 2014, Chinese hardware giant Lenovo has struggled to turn a profit from datacenter sales, even as it expanded its business into storage, networking, and selling to hypersc

Within each scenario, evasion strategies are represented as executable Python programs that implement packet and protocol manipulations — from rewriting TCP/IP header fields, to crafting DNS queries that exploit parser ambiguities, to modifying the internal structure of encrypted QUIC Initial packets — while maintaining protocol correctness within tolerable bounds or strategically violating it when beneficial.” The authors tested CircumVolve on simulated censorship tools used by China, Iran, Pakistan, and Kazakhstan, and on virtual private servers deployed on clouds in those countries. Those tests found the median API cost to the first successful evasion was less than $1 in token expenditure costs when using GPT-5.1. The authors acknowledge that operators of censorship infrastructure might be able to observe CircumVolve at work, but feel its relatively small payloads – 80 KB of outgoing and 150 KB of incoming traffic – and 25-45-second pauses between tests might see it fly under the radar. “CircumVolve represents a first step in leveraging LLMs to accelerate the censorship-circumvention lifecycle,” the authors wrote. “By automating the labor-intensive tasks of protocol analysis, implementation, and testing, AI-driven approaches make studying circumvention capabilities far more accessible to the comparatively under-resourced Internet freedom community [and] demonstrates how AI-assisted systems can narrow the resource gap between Internet freedom advocates and well-funded censoring states.” Lenovo finally cracks monster datacenter profits Ever since acquiring IBM’s x86 server business in 2014, Chinese hardware giant Lenovo has struggled to turn a profit from datacenter sales, even as it expanded its business into storage, networking, and selling to hyperscalers. The AI boom has finally done what various strategy shifts and waves of hype could not: propel the company’s Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) to a $1 billion quarterly profit. In its Q2 results announcement [PDF] last week, the company revealed ISG revenue hit a quarterly record of $11.3 billion, up 178 percent year-over-year, and that lovely big profit. At a time when enterprise hardware supply chains are tight, Lenovo says it was able to increase shipments of x86 servers and even emerge as the largest vendor of such systems with 16 percent market share. Lenovo also claimed it’s moved further ahead as the planet’s premier PC provider, by pointing to 15 percent year-on-year growth for its intelligent devices group where quarterly revenue reached $17.4 billion. The company claims it has 23.8 percent of the PC market and now has seven percent more market share than its closest rival, Apple. The company said premium devices account for 63 percent of its PC business Overall revenue rose 48 percent year over year to $30.24 billion for the quarter. Indonesia’s glaciers are all but gone It may surprise readers to know that Indonesia, the nation that spreads across 17,000 islands in the tropical latitudes of 11°S to 6°N, is home to alpine regions sufficiently high that glaciers can form. Indonesia’s glaciers clung to the top of Puncak Jaya, aka Carstenz Pyramid, a 4,884-meter peak on New Guinea at 4°S. Sadly, an assessment published last week by NASA says the glaciers have probably melted to the point at which not much is left other than a few patches of ice. NASA last week posted images that show glaciers covering 4.31 km2 atop Puncak Jaya in 1988, and another from this year that shows most of that ice is gone. Images from September 2025 apparently showed just .09km 2 of ice remained. “To qualify as a glacier, a body of ice generally has to be thick enough to flow downhill under its own weight, and it needs an area where snow builds up faster than it melts,” NASA’s Kathryn Hansen wrote. “Puncak Jaya’s remaining ice has thinned so much and broken into such small, stagnant patches that it no longer flows.” For what it’s worth, commercial operators run expeditions to Puncak Jaya. Peak-baggers seek it out because some consider it the highest mountain in Australasia/Oceania and therefore one of the “Seven Summits” – the highest point on each continent. The Reg won’t get into the debate about the validity of including Puncak Jaya on that list, but if you fancy some equatorial alpine action your correspondent recently climbed Malaysia’s 4,095m Mount Kinabalu. It’s an overnight walk that requires no technical skills or gear, but definitely demands supple knees . The peak was clearly glaciated in the distant past but snow is now extremely rare on Kinabalu. Australian bank giving away its bug-hunter Here’s an odd one: Australia’s Commonwealth Bank (CBA) created an AI-powered tool to scan its bespoke code for bugs, and has now packaged it as a free release called “CodeCheck.” The bank says analyzes the output of OpenAI’s Codex and Anthropic’s Claude Code with “a consistent process for analyzing code, investigating potential vulnerabilities and providing information to assist engineers.” Apparently, it is “ based on an approach used within CBA, but it is not the same as, and does not represent, the systems, tools or controls CBA uses internally.” The bank posted CodeCheck to GitHub , where it warns the project is “a one-time open-source release for businesses to evaluate” and that it will not actively maintain, update, or support the code. Japan’s space program hands some launches to Mitsubishi Japan’s Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) last week announced it has reached an agreement with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) to take over responsibility for running launches of its flagship H3 rocket when used in certain configurations. The deal means MHI will handle launches for H3s that use a pair of LE-9 liquid-fuel engines alongside two SRB-3 solid-fuel boosters. JAXA will continue running launches that use different, or experimental, configurations. Once JAXA is satisfied those new rigs are reliable, it plans to transition them to private operators, too. ®

item.title: Tinubu’s reforms may be difficult to sustain without re-election — Wike
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said it would be difficult to sustain and stabilise President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms if he fails to secure re-election in 2027. Wike said the initial challenges associated with the removal of petrol subsidy were temporary, arguing that Tinubu should be allowed to complete the foundation he had laid for Nigeria’s economic recovery and prosperity. The minister spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving service at St Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State. He said Nigeria had been facing the threat of economic collapse before Tinubu assumed office, describing the president as courageous for taking difficult decisions. “This country was on the verge of collapse. But by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” Wike said. “And that is why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. He has laid his foundation; now it’s time for prosperity. If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done.” Wike cited what he described as improved stability in the university system, noting that strikes by lecturers over unpaid entitlements, which frequently disrupted academic calendars in the past, were no longer a recurring feature under the Tinubu administration. He also recalled the difficulties pensioners previously encountered in accessing their entitlements, arguing that decisions taken by the president had helped address some of the country’s longstanding challenges. The FCT minister urged Nigerians across religious divides to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, insisting that the president’s campaign would accommodate Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers. “I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters. The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes,” he said. Wike also dismissed claims of religious imbalance in appointments under the Tinubu administration, insisting that Christians had enjoyed greater representation in the current government than in previous administrations. “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” he said. The minister, during the service, announced a donation of N100 million to the church on behalf of the Rainbow Coalition, his friends and associates. The post Tinubu’s reforms may be difficult to sustain without re-election — Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Netflix’s (Very) R-Rated 45-Episode Sci-Fi Anthology Doesn’t Get the Attention It Deserves
item.description: Almost four decades after the film’s release, filmmakers David Fincher and Tim Miller attempted to reboot Heavy Metal , which eventually morphed into the Netflix sci-fi anthology, Love, Death & Robots . Although the series inevitably carries the DNA of Heavy Metal and its contemporaries, Love, Death & Robots carves out its distinct identity over 45 exceptional episodes. While sci-fi is at the heart of these anthology tales, the show blends everything from horror to comedy to complement the bountiful art styles that are a celebration of animation as a medium.

item.title: 'We feel the pain': Pochettino on 4-0 defeat at Liverpool to start Manchester United era – video
item.description: Liverpool thrashed 10-man Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday to climb to fourth in the Premier League. But the defeat left United 19th, only one point above bottom-placed Crystal Palace. There was no new manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino, who saw Leny Yoro sent off in the eighth minute for a last-ditch foul on Alexander Isak. Pochettino accepted full responsibility for the loss, but claimed the dismissal was wrong and United should have had a penalty moments earlier for a Jérémy Jacquet challenge on Bryan Mbeumo. 'It was a desperate take,"' writes Andy Hunter at Anfield. Read the full match report here Continue reading...

item.title: NELFUND considers increase in ₦20,000 student upkeep
item.description: …Sawyer says allowance under review, hints at possible changes By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) is considering an increase in its ₦20,000 monthly upkeep allowance for students amid concerns that rising living costs have reduced its purchasing power. The Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on TVC’s Beyond the Headlines, saying the allowance was under constant review. Although he did not announce a new amount or timeline for any adjustment, Sawyer confirmed that the possibility of an increase was being considered. “Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said. The proposed review comes amid complaints by students that the current allowance is inadequate to meet the rising costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic needs. Sawyer, however, said any increase would have to take into account the fund’s financial capacity and the need to sustain support for all eligible beneficiaries. “What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” he said. Beyond the proposed review, the NELFUND chief disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was considering an intervention to provide students with more substantial financial support to help them complete their academic programmes. He did not provide details of the proposed intervention, including its scope, funding or implementation timeline. “I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” Sawyer said. He also hinted that changes could be introduced in the future, although he gave no definite commitment on when the review would be concluded. “I suspect that if you watch this space, you’ll see some changes coming up in the future,” he added. NELFUND’s proposed review comes as the Federal Government’s student loan scheme continues to expand, with millions of applications received from students seeking financial assistance for tertiary education. According to figures provided by the fund, it has disbursed ₦180.5 billion in upkeep allowances since the scheme commenced in May 2024, while another ₦194.7 billion has been paid to tertiary institutions to cover tuition fees. The combined disbursement of approximately ₦375.2 billion underscores the scale of the programme, which is intended to reduce financial barriers to tertiary education and help students remain in school. The fund has also recorded more than 2.5 million applications and about 1.6 million loan transactions across 320 beneficiary institutions. Despite the programme’s expansion, the adequacy of the monthly upkeep allowance remains a concern for beneficiaries who depend on it to meet their daily expenses. For now, the ₦20,000 monthly allowance remains unchanged, pending any formal announcement by NELFUND or

item.title: Atletico Madrid beat Getafe 3-0 to keep pressure on Barcelona, Real Madrid
item.description: Atletico Madrid stayed on the tail of Spain’s top two with a comfortable 3-0 derby win over Getafe in La Liga on Sunday. Diego Simeone’s side, third, are five points behind leaders Barcelona and two off second-place Real Madrid, who both won earlier this weekend. Alex Baena and Johnny Cardoso’s first-half goals, both set up by Julian Alvarez, got the job done away at the Coliseum stadium in the suburbs south of the Spanish capital. Alex Grimaldo wrapped up the victory in stoppage time with a penalty, after Getafe’s Djene Dakonam was sent off for fouling Alexander Sorloth. “I think the team had a very good, serious game, in defence and attack,” Atletico playmaker Baena told Movistar. “We are focused on our own work, not looking at what Barcelona and Madrid are doing, and that suits us best.” The Rojiblancos moved ahead after 10 minutes, with Alvarez teeing up Baena on the edge of the box to drill home low and hard at the near post. Getafe goalkeeper David Soria saved well from Alvarez and David Hancko but was at fault for Atletico’s second goal. Soria missed his punch from Alvarez’s corner and United States international Cardoso turned home with his knee from point-blank range. Baena smashed over a fine chance for the third after Pablo Barrios played him in behind. Soria denied Baena in the second half and Lee Kang-in fired over as Atletico continued to control the game and defended solidly to keep Getafe, 17th, at bay. Atletico substitute Sorloth should have scored with a few minutes remaining but powered an effort straight at Soria. item.title: Russian ship attacked near Benghazi in suspected drone attack
item.description: Authorities in divided Libya's east said a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi port was hit on Sunday in a suspected drone attack, causing a blast but no casualties. item.title: Watch live on Nov. 23: Amazon launching 1st batch of internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
item.description: null Another batch of Amazon internet satellites will fly on Monday morning (Nov. 23), just eight days after a launch failure doomed 40 of the spacecraft. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana on Monday, during a 29-minute window that opens at 6:09 a.m. EST (1109 GMT; 8:09 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6. Coverage will begin about 30 minutes before launch. An Ariane 6 rocket launches 32 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit from French Guiana on Feb. 12, 2026. (Image credit: ESA/CNES/Arianespace-ArianeGroup/Optique Video du CSG-P. Piron) Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. Monday's mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.

item.title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point. He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors. Diri thanked President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state. He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, noting that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings. President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. He also approved ₦250 million in support for the families of the victims. The post Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Alcaraz downs Zverev to win ATP Finals for first time
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday. After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookended an up-and-down year with a first title at the season-ending showpiece tournament. Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals. With his illustrious compatriot Rafael Nadal never managing to win the season-ending tournament, Alcaraz became the first Spanish champion since Alex Corretja in 1998. “It’s been an amazing week. I couldn’t finish the week in a better way, so I’m really proud,” Alcaraz said after capturing his sixth title of the year. “I’ve been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything. I’m playing great tennis, so for me, lifting this trophy is something that I’ve been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me,” he added of the hamstring issue he suffered earlier in the tournament. A wrist injury had caused Alcaraz to miss a good chunk of the middle of the season and following that victory in Melbourne he failed to add to his seven major titles. But since returning in August, he has enjoyed a blistering end to the year, winning his last 14 matches to capture trophies at the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters for the first time and now the elusive ATP Finals. He lost in the season-ender’s final to Jannik Sinner last year, but with the injured Italian having curtailed his season, Alcaraz found himself again in the Turin title match against a world number one. Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, broke his Grand Slam duck this season by claiming the French and US Opens, catapulting him above Alcaraz and Sinner to the top of the rankings. – Topsy-turvy – The top two seeds in Italy, Alcaraz and Zverev were a cut above the rest all throughout the tournament, both topping their respective pools with three wins from three. The first set of Alcaraz’s semi-final win over Ben Shelton was the only frame either player had dropped all week. Indeed Zverev had marched into the final without dropping a service game, but he was mightily tested straight out of the traps by Alcaraz as the world number three forced three break points in the very first game before the German dug in to hold. Alcaraz was not so wasteful two games later, however, as he broke Zverev to love when the 29-year-old overcooked a mid-court forehand. Zverev forced break-back points in the next game but, after failing to convert, he was left to rue his luck even further as the Spaniard broke to 30 to grow his lead to 4-1. item.content:encoded: Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday. After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookended an up-and-down year with a first title at the season-ending showpiece tournament. Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals. With his illustrious compatriot Rafael Nadal never managing to win the season-ending tournament, Alcaraz became the first Spanish champion since Alex Corretja in 1998. “It’s been an amazing week. I couldn’t finish the week in a better way, so I’m really proud,” Alcaraz said after capturing his sixth title of the year. “I’ve been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything. I’m playing great tennis, so for me, lifting this trophy is something that I’ve been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me,” he added of the hamstring issue he suffered earlier in the tournament. A wrist injury had caused Alcaraz to miss a good chunk of the middle of the season and following that victory in Melbourne he failed to add to his seven major titles. But since returning in August, he has enjoyed a blistering end to the year, winning his last 14 matches to capture trophies at the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters for the first time and now the elusive ATP Finals. He lost in the season-ender’s final to Jannik Sinner last year, but with the injured Italian having curtailed his season, Alcaraz found himself again in the Turin title match against a world number one. Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, broke his Grand Slam duck this season by claiming the French and US Opens, catapulting him above Alcaraz and Sinner to the top of the rankings. – Topsy-turvy – The top two seeds in Italy, Alcaraz and Zverev were a cut above the rest all throughout the tournament, both topping their respective pools with three wins from three. The first set of Alcaraz’s semi-final win over Ben Shelton was the only frame either player had dropped all week. Indeed Zverev had marched into the final without dropping a service game, but he was mightily tested straight out of the traps by Alcaraz as the world number three forced three break points in the very first game before the German dug in to hold. Alcaraz was not so wasteful two games later, however, as he broke Zverev to love when the 29-year-old overcooked a mid-court forehand. Zverev forced break-back points in the next game but, after failing to convert, he was left to rue his luck even further as the Spaniard broke to 30 to grow his lead to 4-1. Zverev wiped out one break but Alcaraz was nonetheless firmly in the ascendancy and pounced for a third time on the Hamburg native’s serve in an entertaining seventh game which saw Zverev dejectedly chuck his racquet to the floor after netting a smash from an Alcaraz tweener lob. A netted backhand by Zverev — his 19th unforced error of the match — on Alcaraz’s first set point then brought an end to a surprisingly sloppy opening frame. Both players exchanged breaks in the second set as it went the distance. The Murcian took a 3-0 lead in the tie-break before Zverev won the next six points to bring up three set points. But the Spaniard struck back to wipe them out before getting a mini-break to bring up championship point on his own serve. The first went begging when he whipped a forehand into the tramlines but he brought up a second with a drop-shot and sealed the title with a backhand. item.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos Is The Big Deal To Me, Says Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has described Lagos State as crucial ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise voters and ensure a higher turnout in the state. Tinubu spoke on Sunday during a prayer session at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos, where he urged them not to generate the maximum win. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door. “Tell them to get, collect their PVC,” he said. The President also urged the attendees at the prayer session that collecting the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) was essential to exercising their democratic rights. “If you are here and you don’t have PVC, you are just here for amala and ewedu,” he told those present jokingly. “If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure. “Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. You have to generate the maximum,” he added. ﻿ Tinubu lost the state to Peter Obi , who was then the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, despite the President’s longstanding political influence in the commercial capital where he served as governor from 1999 to 2007. According to results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. The Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate in the election, Atiku Abubakar, came third with 75,750 votes, while Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party scored 8,442 votes. The results showed that although Tinubu won 11 of Lagos State’s 20 local government areas, Obi secured the overall victory, winning nine local government areas, including Alimosho, Ojo and Oshodi-Isolo. Lagos had 6,214,970 PVCs collected ahead of the 2023 election, the highest number recorded by any state in the country. However, only 1,335,729 votes were cast in the state, comprising 1,271,451 valid votes and 64,278 rejected ballots. Tinubu is seeking to consolidate his political support in the state as he prepares for another presidential contest in 2027, with opposition candidates, including Obi and Atiku, also in the race. The post 2027 Elections: Lagos Is The Big Deal To Me, Says Tinubu appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Sorry, Vice City, but You’re the Most Boring Part of GTA 6
item.description: When Grand Theft Auto 6 was first announced, fans were thrilled at the prospect of returning to Vice City. The Miami-inspired location has always been one of the series’ most memorable locations, its neon-lit streets standing in contrast to the grittiness of Liberty City. While I was as excited as anyone to go clubbing and spend some time on the beach, after 70 hours, GTA 6 has struck me with one surprise thought: Vice City is the least interesting part of Leonida.

item.title: GTA 6's T-shirts Are True Works of Art
item.description: We've known for some time that fashion would be a big deal in Grand Theft Auto 6 . In Rockstar's official promotional materials for the game, both Jason and Lucia were prominently featured wearing stylish clothing, from Lucia's body-hugging gold dress to Jason's slick Miami Vice -inspired aqua sport coat. Even supporting characters like Brian wear Tommy Bahama-inspired aloha shirts yanked straight from the closet of a dapper middle-aged stoner. GTA 6 has drawn praise from all quarters for its scrupulous attention to detail in every aspect of the game, and there's one area the developer went far, far harder than it needed to: the vast and immaculate selection of T-shirts.

item.title: Tinubu Urges APC Leaders To Unite Ahead Of 2027 Elections
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has called on leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to reconcile their differences ahead of the 2027 general elections, underscoring the virtue of forgiveness. He made the call on Sunday at a prayer session organised in his honour by his extended family in Lagos State, urging APC leaders to forgive one another and seek reconciliation. His message was specifically directed at his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Ibrahim Masari, and former defence minister, Abubakar Badaru, both of whom were in the audience at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club, where the President spoke. ﻿ While reacting to reports of a misunderstanding between Governor Dikko Radda and Masari in Katsina State, Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, urged Masari to go back home to reconcile with his governor. “Alhaji Kabiru Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the President’s order. When you finish that, you move to Jigawa. You move to other places and reconcile with them, beg them because we have to reconcile and every anger must dissipate and evaporate,” the President said. He also gave the same order to Badaru, the former governor of Jigawa State. President Tinubu appealed to all APC leaders to set aside personal differences, strengthen internal cohesion, and work collectively to consolidate his administration’s gains ahead of the 2027 elections. He thanked the organisers of the Islamic prayer session and clerics who prayed for him, his administration, and Nigeria. ‘Obstacles Were On Our Way’ He also thanked God for his victory in the 2023 presidential election, despite formidable obstacles which he said “were on our way”. “People cried. People suffered. People died. People had no ₦5 in their pockets because their money was in the bank and they couldn’t get it out. There was also no fuel. “We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun (‘Be, and it becomes’). It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” the President said. The President recalled that he invoked “Emilokan’s spirit (it is my turn) in 2022. “It is now your turn (Eyinlokan) to make the re-election possible,” he was quoted as saying. He appealed to Lagosians to come out en masse on Election Day to exercise their right to vote. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday, but we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door, tell them to collect their PVC. If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6th, and that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” the President said. “We must generate enough votes to overwhelm the opponents,” he emphasised. He reaffirmed his commitment to providing purposeful leadership, strengthening national unity and justice, and building a prosperous country for all Nigerians. Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State described the President as an epitome of justice

People suffered. People died. People had no ₦5 in their pockets because their money was in the bank and they couldn’t get it out. There was also no fuel. “We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun (‘Be, and it becomes’). It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” the President said. The President recalled that he invoked “Emilokan’s spirit (it is my turn) in 2022. “It is now your turn (Eyinlokan) to make the re-election possible,” he was quoted as saying. You must knock on your neighbour’s door, tell them to collect their PVC. If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6th, and that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” the President said. “We must generate enough votes to overwhelm the opponents,” he emphasised. He reaffirmed his commitment to providing purposeful leadership, strengthening national unity and justice, and building a prosperous country for all Nigerians. Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State described the President as an epitome of justice, fairness, equity, and inclusive governance, calling these virtues essential pillars for building a united, peaceful, and prosperous Nigeria. Former Governor of Jigawa, Badaru Abubakar, said northerners appreciated President Tinubu’s support for the late former President Muhammadu Buhari in his 2015 and 2019 election victories. Badaru urged Northern voters to reciprocate the gesture and help the President consolidate the administration’s achievements so far. The chairman of the occasion and elder statesman, 94-year-old Lateef Okunnu, promised to canvass and vote for the President on January 16, 2027. He said the President has done a lot to be re-elected. The elder statesman also emphasised the need to uphold justice, saying that the Tinubu administration is focusing on the economy and infrastructure, especially the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, as well as strengthening the naira and foreign reserves. In their vote of thanks, representatives of the Tinubu family, Rafiu Tinubu and Iyalode Bintu Tinubu, thanked God for the family’s blessings and urged Nigerians to support the President in his determination to deliver the dividends of democracy to the people. Chairman of Lagos State Government House Chapel, Honsu Oluremi, referenced the Bible and urged the people to always pray for leaders’ success. The coordinator of the prayer session and the Grand Chief Imam of Lagos, Sheikh Sulaimon Oluwatoyin Abou-Nolla, while reading from the holy Qur’an, asked Allah to grant the President success in his affairs and good health. The prayer session was attended by Muslim and Christian clerics as well as the governors of Kaduna, Kwara, Ogun, and Imo states. Other in attendance included National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu, Chief of Staff to the President Femi Gbajabiamila, and Lagos Deputy Governor Kadiri Obafemi Hamzat. Also present were the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa; Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa; the Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG), Nasturah Sharriff; the Tinubu family members and party faithful. The post Tinubu Urges APC Leaders To Unite Ahead Of 2027 Elections appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Tinubu’s reforms will be difficult to stabilise if he’s not re-elected - Wike
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has warned that President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms could be difficult to sustain if he fails to secure re-election in 2027. Wike said the president needed another term to consolidate the policies introduced by his administration, arguing that Nigeria was beginning to move towards economic recovery and prosperity despite the initial hardship caused by the reforms. The minister spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving service at St Peter’s Anglican Church in Rumueprikom, Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State. He said Tinubu had taken courageous decisions to address the country’s economic challenges, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy, which he acknowledged came with difficulties for Nigerians. According to Wike, abandoning the president’s policies before their benefits fully materialise could undermine the progress made so far. “This country was on the verge of collapse. item.title: Democrat Hubbard wins North Carolina recount, clinching historic House majority
item.description: Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the US House of Representatives from North Carolina on Sunday after defeating veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee. His victory gave Democrats their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in the 2026 US midterms.

item.title: ‘We need to turn that anger into energy’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 4-0 loss
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card. Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak. United never recovered as Liverpool instantly took advantage when Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick. Defeat leaves United still second bottom of the Premier League and at risk of relegation from the English top flight for the first time since 1974. “It’s so painful, we feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game,” said Pochettino. “We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible. We need to be united, we need to be all together and I think we feel disappointed because it’s clear that after eight minutes, I think, the plan was in the bin.” Isak had taken a heavy touch and the ball appeared to be running through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before contact was made by Yoro. “I’m not going to change what happened and being respectful is always important,” added Pochettino. “At the same time I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.” – ‘Changes the game completely’ – A repeat of United’s 7-0 thrashing at Anfield three years ago appeared on the cards when Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead inside 13 minutes. However, Pochettino’s introduction of Harry Maguire and switch to a back five helped stem the bleeding until teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz rounded off the rout in the second half. “It hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation,” said United captain Bruno Fernandes, who raged against the decision to dismiss Yoro. “There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game,” added the Portuguese international. “It’s not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely.” Victory lifts Liverpool up to fourth in the table and within seven points of leaders Arsenal. Andoni Iraola savoured the adulation coming his way at full-time and believes his side should have run up an even bigger margin of victory. Isak and Bradley Barcola were guilty of wasting a number of big chances either side of half-time. “It’s difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit,” said Iraola. “We have missed some clear chances today. In other games you will remember those chances, but today we’ve controlled the game and everything was happening around the (United) box.” Vanguard News The post ‘We need to turn that anger into energy’ – Pochet

item.title: Gumi calls for removal of Emirs guilty of immoral conduct
item.description: Islamic cleric, Sheikh Ahmad Gumi, has called for the immediate removal of any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct, saying such action is necessary to protect the integrity and credibility of traditional institutions. Gumi made the call in a Facebook post on Sunday, stressing that traditional rulers must uphold high standards of conduct befitting the positions they occupy. He said any Emir found culpable of immoral behaviour should be removed and replaced without delay to preserve the dignity of the traditional institution. “Any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct should be removed and replaced immediately to safeguard the integrity, dignity and credibility of the traditional institution,” he said. The cleric’s position underscores the need for accountability among traditional rulers, whose authority and influence in their communities depend significantly on public trust, moral standing and respect for established customs. Traditional institutions remain important in community leadership, conflict resolution and the preservation of cultural and religious values, making the conduct of their occupants a matter of public concern. The post Gumi calls for removal of Emirs guilty of immoral conduct appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: ‎–Urges APC leaders to forgive one another, unite ahead of 2027 polls ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA –PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu on Sunday in Lagos underscored the virtue of forgiveness at a prayer session organised in his honour by his extended family, urging APC leaders to forgive one another and seek reconciliation. ‎ ‎His message was specifically directed at his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabiru Masari, and former Defence Minister, Alhaji Abubakar Badaru, both of whom were in the audience at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club, where the President spoke. ‎ ‎Apparently reacting to reports of a quarrel between Governor Dikko Umar Radda and Masari in Katsina State, President Tinubu urged Masari to go back home to reconcile with his governor. ‎ ‎ “Alhaji Kabiru Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the President’s order. When you finish that, you move to Jigawa. You move to other places and reconcile them, beg them because we have to reconcile and every anger must dissipate and evaporate,” the President said. ‎ ‎He also gave the same order to Badaru, the former governor of Jigawa State. ‎ ‎President Tinubu appealed to all APC leaders to set aside personal differences, strengthen internal cohesion, and work collectively to consolidate his administration’s gains ahead of the 2027 elections. ‎ ‎The President thanked the organisers of the Islamic prayer session and clerics who prayed for him, his administration, and Nigeria. ‎ ‎He thanked God for his victory in the 2023 presidential election, despite formidable obstacles. ‎ ‎”People cried. People suffered. People died. People had no five naira in their pockets because their money was in the bank and they couldn’t get it out. There was also no fuel. ‎ ‎”We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun (‘Be, and it becomes’). It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” the President said. ‎ ‎The prayer session was attended by Muslim and Christian Clerics as well as Governors of Lagos, Kaduna, Kwara, Ogun, and Imo States. ‎ ‎Other dignitaries in attendance included National Security Adviser Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, Chief of Staff to the President Femi Gbajabiamila, and Lagos Deputy Governor Kadiri Obafemi Hamzat. ‎ ‎Also present were the Minister of Education, Mr Tunji Alausa; Speaker of Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa; the Grand Chief Imam of Lagos, Sheikh Sulaimon Oluwatoyin Abou-Nolla; the Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG), Dr Nasturah Ashir Sharriff; the Tinubu family members and party faithful. ‎ ‎The President recalled that he invoked “Emilokan’s spirit (it is my turn) in 2022. It is now your turn (Eyinlokan) to make the re-election possible.” ‎ ‎He appealed to Lagosians to come out en masse on Election Day to exercise their right to vote. ‎ ‎”The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday, but we cannot take it for granted.
